News.title: Horror as boy, seven, stabs to death his aunt, 49, ‘to protect his mum’ during a row at home in France
News.content:
KNIFE TRAGEDY Horror as boy, seven, stabs to death his aunt, 49, ‘to protect his mum’ during a row at home in France







Next

A SEVEN-YEAR-OLD boy is suspected to have stabbed his aunt to death after overhearing an argument about hair straighteners.

The child reportedly told cops he had been defending his mum when he allegedly stabbed the 49-year-old relative in the throat.



The horror killing took place around 4.30am on Friday in the Paris suburb of Saint-Maur-des-Fossés.

Cops initially went after a man who had been seen brandishing a baseball bat nearby.



But according to Le Parisien, the young boy confessed to killing his aunt, saying: “Yes, it’s me.

“I don’t want to go to prison. I don’t want you to put my mother in prison, I defended my mum.”

Police arrived at the scene to find a woman lying on the street as hero bystanders tried desperately to save her life.

Paramedics attempted to resuscitate the woman, but she was pronounced dead at the scene around 5.17am suffering severe blood loss.

Cops questioned a man with a baseball bat, only to discover he had nothing to do with the crime.

In fact, he had run out of his house armed after hearing the woman’s screams as she lay injured in the street.



The dead woman’s sister then approached police with her son, explaining the horror.

She told cops that she had had a row with her sister, who had been staying over, about hair straightening before “the argument escalated” according to a police source.

Then her seven-year-old son allegedly grabbed a knife hidden in the bathroom and stabbed his aunt in the throat.

The mum said her sister exclaimed: “Your son stabbed me.”

She then ran into the street, shouting “help me”, witnesses said, before collapsing and later dying of her injuries.



The young boy and his mother were taken to hospital.

A police source said the boy’s dad arrived at the scene and reassured him.

He reportedly told the child: “You wanted to defend your mother, it’s okay, you did the right thing, it was an accident.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The prosecutor’s office told Franceinfo there would be “no communication before the beginning of next week, in order to protect the investigation“.

Local media reported that the mum was taken into custody and the child is set to be questioned.

News.title: ‘Generous’ dad, 63, was mauled to death by shark in savage attack as rare ‘catch-and-kill’ order issued for beast
News.content:
Next

AN URGENT hunt is ongoing for a great white shark after a swimmer was mauled to death in Australia.

Greg O’Neill, 63, has been named as the victim of Friday morning’s attack at Sorrento, in Perth’s north, which has now resulted in a rare catch-and-kill order.



Beachgoers watched in horror as the large beast sank its sharp teeth into him, comparing it to “a scene from Jaws, where the body is flicked around like a ragdoll”.

The massacre happened at around 10.30am, as Greg was swimming 50ft from the shore.



Tributes have been paid to the “generous and devoted family man,” who loved the ocean and was known as a “passionate swimmer,” ABC reported.

“Our family is deeply shocked and devastated by the terrible tragedy that took the life of father, grandfather-to-be, brother, uncle, husband and friend, Greg James O’Neill,” his family said in a statement.



“He was a generous, devoted family man that gave his children so much love, care and opportunity.

“Greg loved the ocean and was known as a passionate swimmer, sports lover, dedicated worker and an all round generous, witty guy.

“The kind thoughts and support from everyone who has reached out are deeply appreciated.”

Western Australia Police have since shut Sorrento and the surrounding beaches as the search operation continues.



Fisheries Minister Jackie Jarvis announced the extraordinary measures, but stopped short of ordering a widespread cull.

“Given the shark had been positively identified, remained in the vicinity following a fatal attack, and was considered to pose an ongoing threat, I authorised Fisheries officers to destroy the shark if it could be captured,” she said.

It is believed that this is the first time in 10 years that the ministry has issued such an order.



“I don’t want to give people a false sense of security. I cannot mitigate all risks,” Jarvis added.

So far, efforts to capture the beast remain unsuccessful.

A shark expert has been drafted in by police to investigate how and why the attack may have occurred, 9News reported.

Witnesses described the attack as “gruesome,” adding that Greg was mauled in the water.

“I am a nurse, so I mean I obviously see a lot of gruesome stuff, but to see somebody being mauled to death in the water in front of me is pretty hard to clock,” one woman said.



Jacqui Rapaic, who was walking on the beach with a friend, said: “My friend said, ‘Jac, I think there’s been a shark attack’ and I looked out to the ocean and I could see a pool of blood.”

She said she believed two men had been swimming but only one of them had made it back to shore.

It comes just days after a surfer was mauled further up the coast.

On Monday, surfer Mel Ismail, 56, was attacked by a shark off the waters of Glenfield Beach in Geraldton.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He was dragged to shore by another surfer, Shannan Dunn, but suffered horror injuries to his right leg which had to be amputated below the shin.



A member of the public had reported seeing a 2.5 metre-long shark off the beach earlier that day.

News.title: Who is Putin’s mysterious bodyguard? The buff Russian pin-up and ice hockey elite always in tyrant’s shadow
News.content:
Next

DUBBED Vladimir Putin’s very “own 007”, Anton Afinogenov follows the tyrant like a shadow.

But strangely little is known about the buff Russian pinup who doubles as a sportsman on Putin’s elite ice hockey team.



Snapped in the background of high profile meetings or spotted lurking in the midst of crowds, Afinogenov has skilfully maintained a low profile.

But now the tall, stern faced figure has had his cover blow – by fan pages of Russian women ogling and fantasising over him.



A Moscow security source said: “He is clearly highly trusted by Putin who has his favourites among bodyguards.

“But the president cannot be happy at the superstar status ‘Hunky Anton’ is getting online.

“After all, Putin was a KGB spy and he knows the role is to be unseen and unheard.”

Despite thousands of fans on social media – who even appear to have mocked up pictures of him topless – his age, rank, hometown and education have all managed to remain tightly under wraps.

Swooning fan pages refer to the Presidential Security Service (SBP) officer as “AA” – often matched with a bear emoji.

Comments on fan sites include: “He looks so charming when he smiles; the dimples in his cheeks make him look even better… It’s just so sweet.”



Others swoon that the Putin protector is “walking testosterone” who must have been “created by God”.

Online speculation has linked Afinogenov’s looks to top secret “biotechnological enhancement” programmes.

The alleged projects have been rumoured to create genetically and psychologically modified soldiers.



One woman even urged Putin to elect Afinogenov as successor amid Russia’s ongoing presidential elections.

The woman posted: “I’m voting for him! Come on, Vladimir Vladimirovich [Putin]—seriously, think about a successor. You know the birth rate would skyrocket.”

Putin has already promoted a former bodyguard as a potential successor.

Afinogenov’s predecssor, meanwhile, did not attract a bear emoji but saved Putin from a rampaging brown bear, and was handsomely rewarded.

Ex-bodyguard Col-Gen Alexei Dyumin, 54, now a top Kremlin aide and secretary of the State Council, fired his service gun to scare away the beast.



He is tipped by some analysts to succeed Putin and is seen as backed by the ruler’s lover Alina Kabaeva, 43.

But the public appear to think Dyumin has lost his moment – perhaps to Afinogenov.

“Afinogenov is one of the most visible members of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s security detail,” said one account.



“His presence does not go unnoticed: his imposing physique, constant awareness of his surroundings and calculated movements have made him a recurring figure in official photographs and press footage.”

Weighing more than 100kg and “heavily muscled”, the account claims Afinogenov has paramilitary training and experience in martial arts – a discipline closely associated with the Russian security services.

“The story has even prompted comparisons with action-film characters, reinforcing the idea of a ‘supersoldier’.”

The first sighting of Afinogenov was in July 2011, though he may have been at Putin’s side even earlier.

He wasn’t outed until March 2025 when independent news outlet, Dossier Centre listed bodyguards with clearance and trust to guard Putin on foreign trips.



Based on official photo archives, the outlet identified Afinogenov as one of nine bodyguards to most frequently accompany Putin on trips over the past year.

Others included Alexander Gorelikov, Anatoly Kochkin, Konstantin Panin, Maxim Stepanov, Dmitry Fomin, Yaroslav Chubko, and Yuri Shchurov.

8 Credit: East2West

While the Dossier Centre managed to uncover information on almost all of Putin’s travel squad, not a single detail was recorded for Afinogenov.



In recent years, members of this close group have been appointed to leadership positions in both the Federal Protective Service (FSO) and other high ranking government agencies.

Much of what’s been revealed about the elite Presidential Security Service comes from the “Beyond Russia” website, run by a state-funded operation.

The website says Putin’s bodyguards are hand-picked for qualities including “operational psychology,” physical stamina and the ability to withstand cold and not sweat in heat.

Each guard is reportedly issued a special briefcase to serve as a shield to protect Putin.

They also reportedly carry Russian-made, 9 mm SR-1 Vektor pistols loaded with armor-piercing bullets.



Before Putin travels, advance teams scout out his destination, checking to see how the public will likely respond and even tracking the weather forecast.

Jamming devices are installed in a bid to prevent remote detonation of bombs while technicians surveil cellphones and other devices in the area.

It comes as paranoid Putin bolstered his personal protection squad in recent weeks amid fears of an imminent assassination plot.

The despot now has over 800 elite security forces watching his every move after ordering the number to be increased to 812 from 785, according to a draft decree.

It marks the fourth time Putin has reinforced his security team since he launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.



Before the tyrant launched his full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the central office of the FSO hadn’t increased for almost 13 years.

Putin is the top priority of the FSO alongside his family and closest allies in his inner circle such as the prime minister and defence minister.

Hundreds of staff working close to Putin have even been banned from using mobile phones or other internet-connected devices while around the tyrant, anti-Kremlin reports claim.

Even smart watches have reportedly been blacklisted since around mid-April, according to sources speaking to the Telegram channel Mozhem Obyasnit.

FSO officers also have security systems installed in their homes so other officers can monitor them to ensure they aren’t meddling with a paranoid Putin.



Some of the most senior FSO members have even been spotted wearing disguises to blend into the background of Putin’s annual events.

The rapid increase in FSO agents protecting Putin comes as the despot continues to fear for his life.

In June, he ordered his two eldest daughters to move into his highly guarded forest bunker palace with him for their safety.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He also ordered urgent checks on Russia‘s complex web of surveillance cameras, fearing it could be hacked by his enemies.

His reaction came after Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was taken out by the US and Israel after security cameras were hacked in the rogue nation to track his location.

News.title: French presidential hopeful & Macron’s heir says Britain should join ‘United States of Europe’ in snub to Brexit
News.content:
STATE OF AFFAIRS French presidential hopeful & Macron’s heir says Britain should join ‘United States of Europe’ in snub to Brexit







Next

EMMANUEL Macron’s heir says Britain should join the “United States of Europe” in a massive snub to Brexit.

Gabriel Attal, a frontrunner to succeed French President Mr Macron in 2027, wants a group of perhaps eight or 10 countries to bind together in an audacious plan.



The 37-year-old’s proposal would see member states bind themselves together with common debt, common taxes and labour rules.

However, in a break with the current Brussels model, the union would operate under a directly elected president, according to Mr Attal.



He is also pitching France’s atomic arsenal as the “new European nuclear umbrella”, warning that reliance on American military defence is no longer safe.

Attal said the current 27-member EU model had “reached its limits” amid pressure from “continent powers” such as the US and China.



Attal, who previously called for the UK to rejoin the EU, is dangling a path back into an alliance far more integrated than the union Brits voted to leave.

The United Kingdom officially left the European Union on January 31, 2020 after the country historically voted for Brexit.



But Attal has now said: “I hope that one day the United Kingdom will find its place again in this adventure if it freely chooses to join it.”

The 37-year-old – who made history in 2024 as France’s youngest prime minister – is locked in a brutal dogfight with former premier Édouard Philippe for the centrist crown in next year’s French presidential election.

But his radical European plan faces fierce resistance from EU capitals determined not to hand more powers to Brussels – even if Mr Attal wins the French presidency.

Shared debt remains a massive red line in Germany and the Netherlands, while few capitals will willingly surrender tax powers they have closely guarded for decades.

But Attal insists a core group of member states should forge ahead regardless.



However, smaller nations fear being relegated to second-class status in a two-speed Europe.

His view of a European future is even more radical than that of Mr Macron and European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen.

Mr Macron has never demanded a federal state, focusing instead on European “strategic autonomy” to break dependence on Washington.

The current French PM mounted a similar push for closer European integration after unveiling the Spitzenkandidat system in 2019.

But he ended up backing von der Leyen’s commitment to give member states control over who should head the European Commission.



That stance clashes directly with Attal’s demand for a directly elected president.

While Mrs von der Leyen once championed a federal “United States of Europe”, she backed away from the phrase after taking office.

But Attal has torn into her record, dismissing her state of the union speech as “too little, too late” and declaring Europe must go “faster and further”.

Meanwhile, France could soon turn in a different direction if Marine Le Pen secures the keys to power in 2027.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Opinion polls suggest Ms Le Pen, who was almost banned from standing in 2027, is well-ahead of her rivals.



Recent surveys found that the four-time National Rally contender is at least 10 points clear of Mr Attal in head-to-head polling.

News.title: Shocking moment thugs try to storm nightclub & batter down doors with metal railings after being denied entry
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment thugs attempt to storm a nightclub with metal railings after they were denied entry.

Five men attempted to smash down the doors of Ovation nightclub in Maidstone, Kent, in scenes of chaos last year.



In shocking CCTV footage, the yobs can be seen violently kicking doors and windows at around 1am on September 28.

They then resort to hurling metal security barriers and other objects in an attempt to break through but failed to do so.



During the carnage, the thugs appeared to hit each other with the metal railings a number of times.

Members of staff were injured during the violence with more than £2,000 in damages inflicted on the venue.

The group had assaulted the staff after one of the thugs was denied entry and forcibly removed.

Ethan Beaney, Joshua Fennessy, Arthur Hicks, Dre Mitchell, and Jamie Walker have now been sentenced at Maidstone Crown Court.



Officers were called to the nightclub in the early hours to reports of “violent disorder”.

Three of the group had been arrested after the incident with the remaining two arrested the following day.

They were all ordered to pay £657 in compensation and were sentenced to 12 months and 3 weeks behind bars, suspended for 18 months, reports The Telegraph.

Two of the group – Fenessy and Walker – were also convicted of possessing a Class B drug and sentenced to a further 21 days.

The Crown Prosecution Service posted the dramatic footage online of the moment the group “besieged” the venue.



“The group assaulted the staff after Hicks was denied entry and forcibly removed from the club,” they said.

“Members of staff sustained injuries and total damages to the venue amounted to more than £2,000.

“The charges they were convicted of include affray, criminal damage and possession of a controlled drug.”

News.title: Man, 31, trapped in baby’s body stopped growing before turned one – people travel from across the world for his blessing
News.content:
Next

PEOPLE from across the world have flocked to a remote village in northern India to seek blessings from a man whose parents say is the “incarnation of God”.

At first glance, Manpreet Singh looks like a happy toddler who responds to his mother’s words with a wide smile.



But a closer look reveals he is an adult trapped inside a pint-size body.

Manpreet, from Ramdittewala Village in Punjab, northern India, is a 31-year-old man.



He stands just 23 inches tall and weighs 7.5kg. He cannot talk or walk.

He suffers from an unknown condition that stunted his growth both physically and mentally a year after his birth, but his parents believe that Singh is gift from God.

“We had never heard of a child like him before or had seen anyone like him but we have accepted him as a God’s gift…he is a Sant (saint), an incarnation of God,” Manjeet Kaur, his mother, told The Sun.

Manpreet was born to Jagtar Singh, 54, a private driver and Manjeet, 50, in 1995, four years after their marriage.



Manpreet’s unique appearance initially drew taunts by villagers who would look down at him and his parents. But over the years, he has become famous in the region.

People from far and wide visit the family to seek his blessings, Jagtar said, adding that because of Manpreet, the family has flourished.

He said: “We receive calls and messages from people from around the world. They come to see him and seek his blessings.

“They believe that he fulfils their wishes. They give him donations, sweets, and fruits. Wherever he goes, he gets love from people.”

The parents also take Manpreet to religious congregations where devotees stand in long queues to seek his blessings.



Manjeet said: “At gatherings, he gets so many donations that we have to get security.

“People stand in special queues to get his blessings. He enjoys meeting them, he smiles and waves at them.”

Manjeet said she was unable to conceive and had sought medical help but “their little miracle” arrived after visiting a Hindu temple where she prayed for a child.



Manpreet was born a healthy 3.5 kg baby at home and had a normal growth until 10 months.

“The pregnancy was perfectly normal. I did not undergo an ultrasound and gave birth at home. For the first ten months, his growth was normal,” Jagtar said.

“But after that he suddenly stopped growing. His skin was translucent and red just like a newborn baby, we could see blood flowing through his veins and his limbs were squashy,” he added.

The parents say they consulted about a dozen doctors across the state but none could diagnose their son’s condition.

When medicines did not work, the couple, who are Sikhs but are devout devotees of Hindu gods, took him to several temples and religious figures seeking a miracle but they were told that he is special.



“The doctors said he might have hormonal issues. They gave medicines but he did not respond to them. Instead, he would fall sick every time we gave him medicines,” Jagtar said.

As he cannot walk or move on his own, Manpreet is mostly held in the arms of his parents like a toddler, or left on the bed where he plays with tiny musical instruments.

He requires round-the-clock care which his two younger siblings, sister Jaspreet Kaur, 28, and brother Mangaldeep Singh, 16, help with.



“We have dedicated our lives to taking care of him. There is one person devoted to him at all times,” Jaspreet said.

“His needs are like a baby. We feed him, change his clothes, bathe him. We don’t go anywhere without him. We have been doing this for the last three decades and will do it forever.”

“He cannot speak but he makes signs with his fingers…he tells us how many chapatis (flat bread) he wants to eat,” Jaspreet said, adding, “he doesn’t talk but I understand his language.”

His tiny size means that the parents have to customise his clothes.

“We buy 7.5m cloth for his tunics. He mostly wears black and red,” Jagtar said.



But the parents say their son has changed their lives dramatically.

“Ever since he has come into our lives, we have flourished,” Jagtar Singh said.

He added: “We have got this big house, a car all because of him.

“I had been working for 30 years but we had only a one-room house, not even a kitchen.

“I had a bicycle but because of him, we now have a two-storey house and own a car.



“We believe that he is a form of Lord Shiva and we have dedicated our lives to take care of him.”

The parents, who have made peace with his rare health condition, wish to build a prayer hall for him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Manjeet said: “We have accepted his condition, we are not hoping for any medical miracle.

“We rather want people to come forward and help us build a dedicated prayer hall for him where his devotees could come, sit and meet him.”

News.title: Tehran calls on Iranians to ‘sacrifice their lives’ as thousands flood capital’s streets in regime’s major rally
News.content:
Next

TEHRAN has called on its people to “sacrifice their lives for Iran” as it rallied hundreds of thousands of civilians in a government-organised show of defiance.

Gun-toting regime loyalists marched through the streets of the capital yesterday in an attempted show of force, with authorities claiming more than 300,000 people joined the march.



The regime’s largest demonstration since the US-Israel war on Iran came as its leaders called on its people to give their lives for their country.

The rally was called “Janfaday-e Iran” or “ones who sacrifice their lives for Iran” and was orchestrated as a show of force for the repressive regime.





A huge recruitment drive has been calling up Iranians to take up arms as the country’s economy flounders under the US blockade of its ports.

New volunteers will be trained with assault rifles after security forces gunned down tens of thousands of its own civilians during anti-government protests at the start of the year.



The new head of the Basij, Hossein Taeb, the bloodthirsty IRGC‘s volunteer wing, claimed new recruits will be ready for a “full-fledged defence” of their country.

He said the new volunteers would be a “nightmare” for Iran’s enemies and vowed to repeat the state-backed demonstration in cities across the country.

IRGC boss General Hassan Hassanzadeh said more than 600,000 Iranians had already signed up for the military-training campaign.



He claimed more than a million could take part.



Hardliners trampled American and Israeli flags chanting “Death to the US” and “Death to Israel”.

They even dragged sick coffins adorned with pictures of Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu, after repeated threats on the leaders’ lives.

Demonstrator Marzieh Afaghi, 24, declared: “I am here to tell (U.S. President Donald) Trump that we Iranians have no fear about his threats against our homeland.”

She said: “No one in history could invade Iran and remain there.”

Regime enforcers paraded military equipment through the streets including anti-aircraft batteries and huge machine guns.



It comes as disturbing satellite pics revealed that Iran is rapidly rebuilding a nuclear base just months after Israeli forces blitzed the bunker.

Bulldozers, cranes, concrete mixers and dump trucks can be seen swarming around the sprawling Taleghan 2 facility.

New concrete defences are also springing up around the facility in anticipation of another attack, according to analysis by David Albright, a former UN nuclear weapons inspector.

Israel first bombed the site back in October 2024 before blasting it again in March.

The Washington-based institute described the development as “deeply concerning” because of the base’s previous role in nuclear weapons research.



The bunker formed part of Iran’s secret Amad programme – a plot to develop nukes in the early 2000s.

US intelligence believes the scheme shut down in 2003 – but experts say the bunker still houses a special chamber reinforced for explosive nuclear experiments.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The construction came as Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping blocked a UN motion to monitor whether Iran is violating its pact not to develop the deadly weapons.

News.title: Brit tourist, 60, dies after being pulled unconscious from sea at Greek holiday island
News.content:
HOLIDAY TRAGEDY Brit tourist, 60, dies after being pulled unconscious from sea at Greek holiday island







Next

A BRITISH man has died after being pulled unconscious from the sea on the Greek island of Crete.

The 60-year-old was holidaying on the busy beach of Kato Gouves, in the municipality of Hersonissos, when the tragedy happened.

The alarm was raised when he was spotted in the water and emergency services raced to the scene.



He was taken to the nearby Venizelio Hospital where he was pronounced dead.



The Heraklion Port Authority has ordered an autopsy to determine if the tourist died from a pathological cause or from drowning.

The man has not yet been identified. An investigation into the incident has been launched.

His death comes just weeks after another Brit, 34, died after being pulled from the sea in critical condition in Greece.

He was rescued from the waters after getting into difficulty in Zante.

Bystanders raised the alarm when they saw he was in distress, but the man later died at the General Hospital of Zakynthos.

It comes as a 17-year-old British tourist died after diving into dangerous waters in Crete.

The teen was swimming in the sea when they suddenly started screaming for help in Chania in June.



Six lifeguards rushed to the scene and managed to pull one of the boys out from the rough waters.

But the second boy tragically drowned before he could be rescued.

Greece recorded 376 drowning deaths in 2025, compared to 395 in 2024, according to data from Safe Water Sport.

Of these, 357 deaths occurred at sea, compared to 388 in 2024.

Another 19 deaths took place in inland waters such as rivers, lakes, and pools – up from 7 in 2024, marking a worrying increase in that category.



The data also showed that eight out of 10 people who drown at sea are over the age of 60.

News.title: 'Labour cannot let hope of two-state solution disappear'
News.content:
'Labour cannot let hope of two-state solution disappear'

'Labour got it badly wrong in stubbornly refusing to join calls for a ceasefire early on in the hostilities', former shadow Health Secretary Jonathan Ashworth writes

View 2 Images Former shadow Health Secretary Jonathan Ashworth backed a two-state solution (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham entered Downing Street fizzing with ideas to make life better. He’s cutting VAT on energy bills. There are new efforts to create good industrial jobs across the North and Midlands. Ministers will finally fix care services for those in the throes of dementia.

‌



This government has a clear Labour mission. The public are now giving Labour a second chance.

‌



In the coming days at the UN, Andy Burnham must bring the same fizz, mission and focus to world affairs as well. It’s a daunting task.

‌



Brexit was a hammer blow to our living standards. We need to foster more cooperation with our European partners, not less. Ukraine deserves our ongoing, rock-solid support.

The international community must help end the brutal civil war in Sudan. A coordinated humanitarian response to the devastating Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is needed.

View 2 Images Jonathan Ashworth praised Labour bringing in sanctions on settlements (Image: Tim Merry)

‌



We’re seeing how shipping blockages push up energy and food bills so we all want to see a sustainable end to conflicts.

Labour is best when it's boldest with values at the heart of policy. That’s especially true in foreign policy. This week Andy Burnham, Ed Miliband and Louise Haigh showed bold Labour leadership.

October 7th was a despicable, murderous terrorist atrocity. The rise in vile, frightening antisemitism on our streets is an evil that must be defeated.

‌



I’ve always supported a two-state solution where a secure Israel alongside a viable Palestinian state live side by side in peace.

Labour got it badly wrong in stubbornly refusing to join calls for a ceasefire early on in the hostilities. Frankly I couldn’t look my constituents in the face who were so angry at the Labour leadership’s position.

I know critics will rightly remind me I went along with Labour’s abstention in Parliament. Though I did want Labour to support a ceasefire and argued internally for one, the leadership took a different view. I wasn’t happy with it but also I didn’t want to undermine our chances of ridding the country of the Tories by causing division so close to a general election.

‌



What has been allowed to unfold in Gaza has been shameful. Meanwhile settlement expansion and settler violence in the occupied West Bank everyday undermines any two-state solution.

As a member of Labour Friends of Palestine, I visited the West Bank twelve years ago. What I witnessed will always stay with me.

Andy Burnham made the right call in imposing a ban on trade in goods from these illegal settlements. Labour can’t allow hope to fully drain away from the possibility of a lasting peace through a two-state solution.

‌



'Poetry helping me recover from stroke'

In January an unexpected lightning bolt hit me when I suffered a stroke.

I’ve used Lego and piano playing to get the movement back in my left arm. The amazing thing about the brain is that it can rewire itself post stroke. The boffins call it neuroplasticity in fact.

But stroke recovery isn’t just a physical journey. One in three stroke survivors will experience severe depression.

‌



As an MP fighting for mental health care was a passion of mine and I’m still campaigning.

To help me through the troughs I’ve returned to my love of poetry. Every Sunday on instagram I ask for poetry and recite my favourite poems from Shakespeare to WB Yeats. Tune in and let me know what you would like me to recite.

'Sagal Abdi-Wali is an inspiration'

As a Leicester MP I took pride in helping families fleeing persecution settle in the city. Labour’s candidate in the Holborn by election, Sagal Abdi-Wali escaped war in Somalia arriving in Camden as a child refugee. She has given so much back to Camden as a community activist and councillor. Her story is an inspiration and if elected as their MP will do Camden proud.

Article continues below

'We need more trade unionists in key public roles'

Tory politicians got hot under the collar complaining that TUC boss Paul Novak was taking up a role with the Bank of England. They forgot trade unionists have been involved with the Bank for donkey’s years. For too long wages have been allowed to be squeezed, we need more trade unionists in key public roles, not less.

News.title: 'Harmful' health warning issued to parents with babies suffering from colic
News.content:
'Harmful' health warning issued to parents with babies suffering from colic

The MHRA acknowledged it could be 'distressing for babies and their families'

View Image Colic can be distressing for babies - and parents

A health warning is being issued to parents of babies that are suffering from wind or colic. The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) issued the warning as some people use colic relievers to alleviate symptoms in their children.

‌



The MHRA acknowledged that wind or colic can be 'very distressing' for babies. However, it urged parents not to use wind or colic relievers, claiming that they could be 'harmful'.

‌



It also said that there was 'not enough evidence' to suggest that the relievers even worked. Also known as rectal catheters, they are also used to ease constipation. They work by using hollow plastic tubes with a stopper which are inserted into the baby's bottom.

‌



"Parents and carers are advised not to use wind and colic relievers in babies," an MHRA post said. "Wind or colic can be very distressing for your baby. However, we do not recommend the use of wind or colic relievers.

"We have reviewed these products and found there is not enough evidence that they work and there are concerns that they could be harmful.

"Speak to your health visitor or a healthcare professional for advice on the safest and most effective way to manage your baby’s wind and colic."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

What else does the MHRA say?

An MHRA statement said: "Following a review of available evidence and expert clinical advice, the MHRA has concluded that there is insufficient evidence that these devices work as intended. The MHRA is also concerned about the potential risks associated with their use.

"Please note this advice is not applicable for rectal catheters that are used by healthcare professionals in specialist areas such as Hirschsprung’s, meconium ileus, or gastroschisis.

‌



"The MHRA is advising that parents and caregivers do not use or recommend the use of these products in infants, and that any products already purchased should be disposed of.

"While there have been no confirmed reports of serious injury, the safety and benefits of these products remain uncertain. There are concerns that using these products could make it harder to detect underlying conditions that may require medical attention. Experts also considered the potential risk of injury to the bottom, including tearing or perforating the inside of an infant’s bottom, which could have serious consequences."

'Distressing for babies and their families'

Dr Alison Cave, MHRA chief safety officer, said: “We understand that colic and digestive discomfort can be distressing for babies and their families. We are advising against the use of rectal catheters in babies because there is not enough clinical evidence to support their safety and effectiveness.

‌



“Parents and caregivers should seek advice from a healthcare professional and follow the NHS guidance if they are concerned about their baby.”

Anyone who experiences a problem with a medical device or suspects that their child has had a side effect related to the use of rectal catheters should report it directly to the MHRA Yellow Card scheme.

What is colic?

The NHS describes colic as when a baby cries a lot but there's no obvious cause. It's a common problem that should get better by around 3 or 4 months of age. Doctors often use the rule of three - a baby crying for more than three hours a day, three days a week for three weeks.

News.title: Man stabbed to death on London 'Millionaires' Row' as Met Police launches murder probe
News.content:
Man stabbed to death on London 'Millionaires' Row' as Met Police launches murder probe

A murder probe is underway after a 28-year-old man was found with stab wounds on a 'Millionaires Row' in Clerkenwell, London, and tragically died the following day

View Image The man was found injured in Clerkenwell, London (Image: Google Maps)

Police launched a murder probe after a man was stabbed to death on a "Millionaires' Row" in London.

‌



Officers raced to Lloyd Baker Street in Clerkenwell at around 11:20pm on Wednesday and found a 28-year-old man with stab wounds, the Metropolitan Police said. He was rushed to hospital by paramedics but tragically died on Thursday.

‌



The man's next of kin have been informed, and are being supported by specially trained officers.

‌



No arrests have been made, the Met Police said. Detectives are urgently appealing for members of the public with any information about the incident to contact them.

Lloyd Baker Street is among the more affluent residential addresses in Clerkenwell, featuring Grade II listed Georgian terraced houses which sell for as much as £2.25million. Floral tributes have been placed on the street by the victim's loved-ones.

‌



A Section 60 order has also been issued, granting officers enhanced powers to stop and search people and vehicles. This applies to the Caledonian Road, Clerkenwell and Hoxton areas. The order ran from 4pm on Friday September 18 to 6am on Saturday September 19.

Chief Superintendent Jason Stewart, who leads policing in the local area, said: "This is a tragic incident, and our thoughts remain with the family and friends of the young man who has lost his life.

"You can expect to see additional officers in the area providing visible reassurance and working with partners to keep the public safe.

Article continues below

"The victim was found in a residential street, and members of the public may have information of vital importance to our investigation. If you can help, please come forward."

Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101, quoting reference CAD 8475/16SEP. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously via Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: UK weather: Britain facing mega 29C late September heat blast with 24 counties forecast glorious sunshine
News.content:
UK weather: Britain facing mega 29C late September heat blast with 24 counties forecast glorious sunshine

As many as 24 counties could welcome temperatures of 27C or higher, with the hottest areas potentially reaching 29C as a late September warm spell sweeps across parts of Britain

View 2 Images Multiple areas could soon see temperatures in the high 20s (Image: Joe Sene/PA Wire)

Brits could be in for a late September heat blast, with weather maps showing temperatures potentially soaring to 29C in a matter of days.

‌



The ECMWF weather model suggests the hottest conditions will be concentrated across the south and east, but that the warmth could push much further north than is typical for a late-September spell. By September 28, multiple major cities, including London, Birmingham and Cambridge could all climb into the high 20s.

‌



Potential highs of 29C may be seen in Cambridge, Bedford, Peterborough and Northampton, while London and parts of Kent could reach between 26C and 28C. Further north, the warmth could extend towards Sheffield, Lincoln and Hull, where temperatures could also reach the mid-20s or higher.

‌



View 2 Images Highs of 29C could arrive by September 28 (Image: WXCHARTS)

The southwest and areas around Gloucester could see highs of around 27C, although surrounding areas are generally expected to be a little cooler. Wales is set for possible highs of 20C to 22C, while Scotland is expected to remain cooler, with highs broadly around 20C.

The ECMWF weather model suggests up to 24 UK counties could see temperatures of 27C or higher on the evening of September 28. It comes as the Met Office warns the wider period is likely to remain changeable at first, before "periods of drier and more settled weather" return, possibly lasting "a few days".

‌



Temperatures are also expected to be above average overall during this time, the forecast adds.

In its long-range forecast for September 23 to October 2, the Met Office said: "A changeable period is expected, with Atlantic weather systems bringing spells of rain, showers and occasional strong winds.

"The wettest and windiest conditions are most likely across northern and western areas, although stronger winds may at times extend more widely.

Article continues below

"Between these unsettled spells, periods of drier and more settled weather are likely, especially in the south and east, where they may last for a few days.

"Accompanying these may be some overnight fog and frost. Temperatures are expected to be slightly above average overall."

Counties set for 27C or higher on September 28

News.title: Cannabis made to look like sweets and cake being sold online sparks fear for kids
News.content:
Cannabis made to look like sweets and cake being sold online sparks fear for kids

Campaigners have shared their worries that drug dealers advertising sweets and cakes laced with cannabis on social media could be targeting kids

View 5 Images 'Cannaburst' gummies laced with cannabis being advertised on social media (Image: Daily Record)

Drugs being made to look like popular brands of sweets, drinks, cake and even chocolate are being flogged on the internet, with fears they are being "designed to appeal to children".

‌



Dozens of social media pages in Scotland have been found to advertise and post images of cannabis-laced items, with many of imitating popular snack brands. Some of these concerning items include gummies called Cannaburst, imitating the popular Starburst sweets, and even ice cream cones with cannabis-laced Nutella spread.

‌



Campaigners have warned that these drug dealers using branding similar to sweets and snacks was "especially dangerous for children and young people".

‌



Mum met boy on beach holiday then used him to sell cocaine up to 20 times a day READ MORE :

Comical moment bungling crook fails three times to throw £12,000 worth of drugs over a prison wall READ MORE :

View 5 Images Cannabis-laced Nutella cones being advertised online (Image: Daily Record)

Dozens of concerning social media pages and s for fake replicas of brands to sell drugs were discovered, in an investigation by the Daily Record.

One of these included a blue packet of gummies is also branded as "Medicated Jolly Ranchers" which even used the same logo as the American sweet company.

‌



View 5 Images Cannabis-gummies made to look like a popular American sweet (Image: Daily Record)

Another advert even showed a peach lemonade being flogged on the internet with another dealer even creating a hot sauce to be for "Peri-peri chicken", referencing a popular fast food among young people.

The cannabis-laced foods did not stop at packaged goods with one account even trying to sell Oreo cheesecakes, luxury cupcakes and lollipops with the drug.

‌



View 5 Images Peri-peri hot sauce laced with cannabis (Image: Daily Record)

It also advertised a "dopey dipping box" which was styled to look like a sweet treat platter, with tea cakes, fruit and cookies to dip into cannabis blended dips.

Edible cannabis could also pose specific dangers as there is a risk somebody could be taking something more dangerous than cannabis, according to FRANK. The anti-drug service said there had been cases of young people taking what they thought was cannabis edibles but had taken something containing synthetic cannabinoids rather than THC without knowing it, which could cause hallucinations, extreme paranoia and death.

‌



Several campaigners have come out and shared their concerns against the cannabis advertised as sweets and treats on the internet.

View 5 Images Dealers have also been spotted selling drinks on social media (Image: Daily Record)

The CEO of Scottish Families Affected by Alcohol and Drugs, Laura Mahon said: "These products are clearly designed to appeal to children, with the use of branding similar to well-known sweets and snacks.

‌



"We want to see greater action to prevent these products from being advertised and sold online, particularly where content can be seen by young people.."

The With You Charity National Harm Reduction Lead, Gareth Balmer, added: "Some of these products are deliberately designed to look like sweets - especially dangerous for children and young people, who may have no idea what they're taking or how strong it is. We continue to call on social media platforms to strengthen safety measures and remove accounts selling unregulated substances."

A Scottish Government spokesperson said: "While the UK Government is responsible for the regulation of the internet, the Scottish Government shares the concerns of many parents about young people’s access to inappropriate material online.

Article continues below

"That is why we have been clear in our calls for greater controls to reduce online harms to children, and we will work constructively with the UK Government to that end."

News.title: Making a Murderer killers now - prison lovers, brutal backstabbing and freedom bid
News.content:
Making a Murderer killers now - prison lovers, brutal backstabbing and freedom bid

Steven Avery and Brendan Dassey have reportedly turned against each other behind bars, where both field dozens of letters from 'fans'

View 12 Images Steven Avery and Brendan Dassey are both applying to reduce their life sentences (Image: UGC)

It was one of the first ever binge-worthy true crime shows in Netflix history, but the astonishing story of Making a Murderer didn't end when the cameras stopped rolling.

‌



Eleven years on and plenty of failed freedom bits later, its subjects, Steven Avery and Brendan Dassey, are trying a new strategy to get out of prison.

‌



Avery and his nephew Dassey, who are are both serving life sentences for the murder of Teresa Halbach, have applied to reduce their sentences. Court records show that the killers have this month submitted applications to the Governor's Commutation Advisory Board.

‌



Avery has filed at least four major appeal motions against his conviction since his sentencing in 2007, with all of them being denied. The request for a reduced sentence is his last-ditch attempt for freedom as he's ran out of options.

More than a decade on since the 10-part series transfixed audiences across the world, Avery and Dassey's lives are unrecognisable. We look at where they are now...

What happened to Teresa Halbach?

It was Halloween in 2005 when photographer Teresa vanished during an assignment for AutoTrader magazine. The 25-year-old freelancer had been tasked with photographing a minivan at Avery's Auto Salvage in Manitowoc County, Wisconsin. Ran by Allan and Dolores Avery, the couple's sons lived and worked at the junkyard.

‌



This included their son, Avery, who was at that time filing a $36 million civil lawsuit after being wrongfully imprisoned for the 1985 beating and sexual assault of Penny Beerntsen, who was brutally attacked while jogging along the Lake Michigan shoreline. Traumatised Penny, then 36, mistakenly picked Avery out of a line-up, an error that would go on to haunt her.

View 12 Images Teresa Halbach, who was murdered in 2005 (Image: UGC)

In 2003, through DNA testing, the Innocence Project proved once and for all that Avery was not guilty. Instead, the DNA matched Gregory Allen, a known flasher who had gone on to commit other violent assaults.

‌



Survivor Penny would later tell Radiolab that the day she learned she'd misidentified the wrong man was "worse than the day I was assaulted".

Avery, who maintained his innocence, was exonerated and released. Then, on November 5, 2023, two days after Teresa was reported missing by her parents, Tom and Karen Halbach, her Toyota RAV 4 was recovered from under brush at the Avery Salvage Yard, which would have been her last stop of the day.

View 12 Images Steven Avery was wrongfully convicted of the rape of Penny Beerntsen (Image: UGC)

‌



As some 200 police officers combed the yard, charred remains and bone fragments were recovered from a burn pit. Personal items belonging to the University of Wisconsin-Green Bay graduate were also recovered from the sprawling property, including parts of her phone and camera.

On November 15 of that year, Avery was arrested and charged with the murder, kidnapping, sexual assault, and mutilation of a corpse, having already been charged with a weapons violation on November 9.

Avery had been the last person to see Teresa alive, and the evidence against him mounted. Drops of Avery's blood were found in Teresa's car, while her car keys, which contained his DNA, were recovered from his bedroom. Teresa's license plates were discovered in another vehicle at the yard, while a bullet fragment found in the garage had her DNA.

‌



View 12 Images Poster for Making A Murderer, which brought the case to the forefront (Image: UGC)

Avery continued to protest his innocence, and his trial attorneys would later argue that the Manitowoc County Sheriff's Office could have planted evidence to frame him on account of his wrongful conviction lawsuit.

It was suggested that a vial of Avery's blood, which had been stored in an evidence locker since 1985, could have been tampered with, as allegedly evidenced by broken seals and a puncture in the stopper.

‌



In January 2006, DNA testing determined that the remains belonged to Teresa, remembered by loved ones for her sunny disposition. Kate Uttech, a friend from Teresa's student days, told PEOPLE: "She just enjoyed life, she enjoyed new experiences.

View 12 Images Avery was the last person to see Teresa alive (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

"She was always very positive. I don't ever remember her being mad about anything. She just had this positivity about herself. She didn't have a bad bone in her body."

‌



That same month, Avery pleaded not guilty. In February, Avery settled his lawsuit for around $400,000, needing the money to cover the costs of private defence lawyers.

In March of that year, things took a turn when Avery's then 16-year-old nephew, Brendan Dassey, was charged with participating in first-degree intentional homicide, mutilation of a corpse and first-degree sexual assault.

View 12 Images Brendan Dassey, who was 16 years old at the time of his confession (Image: UGC)

‌



The teenager, who had a very low IQ, gave a shocking videotaped confession. Interrogated alone over a 48-hour period, Dassey confessed he had helped Avery rape and murder Teresa.

Dassey told officers that Avery had stabbed Teresa before shooting her five times. He said: "While he was doing that, I wasn't looking because I can't watch that stuff." It was then, Dassey claimed, he and Avery had put Teresa's body on the fire, using her clothes to "clean up some of the blood".

Almost immediately, Dassey retracted his confession, which, many years later in 2016, US Magistrate Judge William Duffin ruled had been coerced, and involuntary on account of his young age, intellectual difficulties, and alleged "inappropriate" conduct on behalf of investigators.

‌



View 12 Images Dassey, who confession was ruled 'involuntary' (Image: UGC)

In a court order, Mr Duffin said: "The investigators … assured Dassey that he had nothing to worry about. These repeated false promises, when considered in conjunction with all relevant factors, most especially Dassey's age, intellectual deficits, and the absence of a supportive adult, rendered Dassey's confession involuntary."

In March 2007, Avery was found guilty of first-degree murder and illegal possession of a firearm. The then 44-year-old was sentenced to life imprisonment that same summer, without the possibility of parole. Dassey, then 17, was also convicted in 2007 and handed a life sentence with no parole for 41 years, right up until 2048. By this point, he'll be nearly 60 years old.

‌



Avery and Dassey's lives in prison

Housed at the Fox Lake Correctional Institution in Wisconsin, after being moved from the maximum-security Waupun Correctional Institution, Avery, now 64, has led an eventful life behind bars, including multiple relationships and engagements.

View 12 Images Convicted killer Steven Avery with his former fiancée, Lynn Hartman (Image: Dr Phil)

Avery was first engaged to supportive fiancée Sandra Greenman, with the pair remaining close friends after their on-and-off-again relationship ended. He then embarked on a brief relationship with Las Vegas legal secretary Lynn Hartman, who got engaged in 2016 after eight months of dating and one in-person visit.

‌



Speaking with the Daily Mail at the time, Avery shared: "I'm happy. She treats me decent, she loves me – she's kind of spoiling me right now. I just want to be happy and enjoy my life. I think I did enough time." Divorced mother-of-four Hartman also told the publication: "Despite all obstacles, and Steven's wrongful conviction and incarceration, we plan to be married shortly after he is released."

Their romance didn't last long, however, and in October 2016, mere days after going public, the couple parted ways, with Avery accusing Hartman of being a "golddigger". Hartman, who received $5,000 for a Dr Phil interview, also turned on her ex-fiance, who she claims demanded "four-hour sex sessions" and referred to her by the crude nickname "my vagina".

View 12 Images Hartman opened up about their romance on an episode of Dr Phil (Image: Dr Phil)

‌



According to Hartman, Avery also spoke badly of his incarcerated nephew, Dassey, allegedly declaring: "F*** Brendan, I don't give a s*** about him. He should have kept his mouth shut."

News of the break-up was shared on Facebook by Avery's loyal ex Greenman who wrote: "She has been in this relationship for money and publicity. His eyes are finally opened!!!"

View 12 Images Avery accused Hartman of being a 'golddigger' (Image: Facebook.com/averydasseyproject)

‌



Speaking with The U.S. Sun in 2024, Greenman declared her enduring loyalty to Avery, while revealing that there was a new woman in his life. She said: "Steven and I are just friends, but I will always stand by him. I have had many people in support groups assume we are back together.

"I am still in contact with him, and visit as much as I can. He's doing pretty good under the circumstances. He has a girlfriend. She doesn't want it made public though. Strange, but her and I are friends. She lives in another state, but is here often. I think she is good for him. I hope so anyway!"

View 12 Images Dassey is now 36 years old, and reportedly harbours doubts over his uncle's innocence (Image: Irish Daily Mirror)

‌



Greenman also previously claimed that Avery received more than 40 letters and photographs of near-naked women every single day after Making A Murderer hit streaming, and thought himself a "Hollywood star."

While he has exhausted his appeals, Avery had maintained his innocence in his recent application. As per documents obtained by FOX11, Avery wrote: "I did not commit this crime. I feel bad for Teresa Halbach's family because they had to suffer such a tremendous loss. But I did not cause their loss."

The Wisconsin man went on to detail his good prison record and the supportive messages he'd received from family and friends. He also shared his hopes of opening his own auto body business, should he ever be released. Dassey, too, continued to assert his innocence, penning: "That day, I came home from school and stayed home all afternoon.

‌



View 12 Images Avery is '100 per cent' guilty say Teresa's relatives (Image: UGC)

"That night, Steven asked me to help him clean his garage floor and put a van seat and tyres on his bonfire. I didn't see or hear anything unusual. If I had I would have told my mom and called police."

According to Dassey, who is now 36 years old, he now harbours doubts over his uncle's innocence. Dassey said: "Now that I'm older, part of me thinks it's possible that Steven might have been involved because of how he treated women." He added: "If I get out I want nothing to do with Steven ever again."

‌



Dassey is held at the Columbia Correctional Institution, the maximum-security Wisconsin prison where, infamously, serial killer Jeffrey Dahmer was murdered. Dassey is said to receive plenty of supportive letters. He also whiles away the hours writing letters, reading and watching television.

Steven Drizin, one of his two lawyers, told People that Dassey’s family members have "been unfailing” in their enduring support for him. Meanwhile, Laura Nirider, Drizin’s co-counsel, remarked that, while “life in prison isn’t easy,” Dassey remains “a hopeful guy". She added: "He’s somebody who throughout all of this still manages to have faith that one day the truth is going to come out.”

While the Netflix documentary Making a Murderer touched upon the potential doubt in the conviction of Avery and Dassey, Teresa's family believes Avery is "100 per cent guilty". Addressing the docuseries at the time, Teresa Halbach’s aunt, Kay Giordana, told People: “He is 100 per cent guilty. No doubt about it."

‌



Meanwhile, Teresa's cousin-in-law, Jeremy Fournier, felt the documentary series to be biased, asserting: “It is so very one-sided…. It seems like there are some shenanigans by the police in there from what I hear and read about, and I can see where people are getting their opinion, but they are only getting one side of the story.”

If you've been the victim of sexual assault, you can access help and resources via www.rapecrisis.org.uk or calling the national telephone helpline on 0808 802 9999
