He blasted home a 39th-minute penalty to take the record before nodding in a Michael Olise cross early in the second half to send Bayern top of the table before the other weekend matches.

The feat stole the spotlight from Olise, who scored his first Bayern hat-trick, and Jamal Musiala, who also scored a goal worthy of winning any game.

“I’m very proud to have now scored 100 and 101 Bundesliga goals. I haven’t been around that long. I’ve loved every second of it,” Kane told Sky Germany. “With Michael, Lucho [Luis Díaz] and Jamal I naturally get chances and today was no exception.

“So I just want to thank the team, the club, the coach, and the staff – everyone who has helped me achieve this. Let’s keep going like this. Scoring more goals in games is obviously a big step. Of course, there have been many important goals among them. I can only say that I’m enjoying every minute of it. Just like today.”

Sports.title: Heat is on Carrick but Wilcox must share blame for Manchester United’s woes
Sports.content:
There was a mix of boos and apathy as Manchester United slumped out of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday in their latest depressing act in domestic cup competitions. A solemn Michael Carrick and his players were the target for the jeers. The director of football, Jason Wilcox, looked unamused on his way out of the directors’ box but he and the hierarchy need to accept responsibility for their actions.

This is the natural course of football, where supporters know what is good or bad and give a rapid opinion to those whose wages they deem they pay. Carrick and his charges are the face of the club, the ones put up to speak with journalists and sent to promote the wares of sponsors.

The head coach is often viewed as accountable for everything, from tactics to transfers, but the picture is more complex.

Carrick returned to United in January, but others have overseen the long-term strategy, within which the head coach sits. Pressure comes with his job, though, and a loss at Fulham on Sunday would significantly increase it.

United’s fanbase is fully aware of those running the club, with regular protests against the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. They realise not everything happening over 90 minutes is the fault of the head coach and those wearing the shirt. The boos are for the one-off performance, the apathy for the bigger picture. It is tough for United supporters to see their club, back in the Champions League, outspent in the summer by promoted sides but this is the reality after years of financial mismanagement. It means the funds available have to be spent wisely.

United being two goals ahead against Brighton after 10 minutes and deservedly losing a game they were barely involved in for the remaining 80 is a strong indication things are not right within the team but Carrick knows this. Brighton were much changed but possess an exciting array of talent acquired from all over the world thanks to clever scouting and recruitment. They signed players from clubs in seven countries this summer, while United made four acquisitions from fellow Premier League clubs. Calculated risks and dynamism are part of the job but rarely seen at Old Trafford. It is somewhat ironic considering the most successful acquisition last summer was Senne Lammens from Royal Antwerp, in terms of price and consistency.

Carrick and Wilcox cannot truly be analysed until the most expensive of the three summer buys, Carlos Baleba, is available because his attributes should solve the lack of mobility. Targeting central midfielders was logical after the exit of Casemiro and inadequacy of Manuel Ugarte, but it was not the only area requiring attention. The overall deficiency of the squad was acknowledged internally but the lack of variety in strengthening felt naive and is proving to be so.

View image in fullscreen Senne Lammens was Manchester United’s most successful signing last year, yet the club chose to invest mainly in Premier League players this summer. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

Buying players from other Premier League clubs is rarely cost-effective but there is a logic to limiting the adaptation time. Given the left-back shortage and Joshua Zirkzee’s inadequacies, sourcing a cheaper midfield option than the £50m Andrey Santos could have been advantageous for the wider health of the team. Someone needs to alleviate the pressure on Carrick by explaining why it was deemed best to spend £155m on three players in the same position. The outside world is left to pontificate, while Carrick creates a plan B when Luke Shaw, as many anticipated, has time out injured.

Wilcox has carried out internal media duties. On 30 October 2025, after three consecutive wins, he discussed the long-term plan, which was derailed by sacking Ruben Amorim just over two months later. Matters were going well when Wilcox opened up to United’s editorial staff but, apart from statements on sackings, he shows no appetite to speak amid downturns.

In Europe, sporting directors talking to the press is normal but the Premier League is yet to catch on, and the silence mounts at United with the team 13th.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wilcox arrived, originally as technical director, from Southampton in 2024 and helped oversee the retention of Erik ten Hag after an eighth-placed finish. Ten Hag was belatedly dismissed for a poor start to the next season. Amorim was hired from Sporting despite his tactics not matching up with the squad available and a lack of finance to provide the overhaul required. United ended 15th and endured a meek Europa League final defeat by Tottenham. When Amorim was dismissed for his shortcomings after 14 months, Wilcox was permitted another chance to rectify the situation.

Carrick is not absolved of criticism; this United team are underperforming and pummelling promoted Ipswich and the Azerbaijan side Sabah cannot mask the disappointing start.

The defence has struggled, conceding seven goals in four Premier League games, and against Brighton the pairing of Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven was bordering on inept. The forward line has looked disjointed.

Wilcox was well respected when working as Manchester City’s head of academy, and those who dealt with him thought he was exceptional and suited to a role at that level. He is scrutinised and criticised for his work at United after moving up the chain. Many on the outside will be frustrated if JJ Gabriel departs but Wilcox would not be culpable, having worked hard to convince the player to stay, including via the teenager’s inner circle.

With power comes great responsibility at United but only Carrick is forced to embrace it. Ten Hag and Amorim have fallen for their failures, while others have been allowed to carry on. Carrick and Wilcox are equally invested in the success of the team but it seems only one will feel the consequences if things do not improve.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola makes Bournemouth return still learning on the job at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Alisson made little attempt to sugarcoat Liverpool’s unbeaten start to the season under Andoni Iraola when analysing the draw against Fulham with the club’s in-house media. “Unbeaten with three draws is not something to celebrate too much with this shirt,” said a peeved Liverpool goalkeeper. “We take the clean sheet but we are not happy at all. We need to aim for big things.”

Big things are the target and big things are expected from a Liverpool side containing three £100m-plus forwards. But the learning curve under the new head coach is proving challenging. As it is for the new head coach, too. Big decisions appear unavoidable.

When Iraola faces his former club Bournemouth on Sunday for the first time since ending his impressive three-year reign there last season, he is likely to know more about the opposition players than his own. “It’s going to be a tricky one because they know very well what we try to do,” Iraola admitted. “But I also know their strengths and weaknesses. It’s going to be strange for me.”

Iraola spent more than two hours debriefing Marco Rose, his successor at the Vitality Stadium, on the Bournemouth squad and staff in June. They had time for a smooth handover because, as Iraola put it, his exit from the club “was so clean” and he decided to stay on the south coast while his two young children finished school. Whether they discussed how Bournemouth became the draw specialists of last season remains private.

No coach or manager oversaw more stalemates in the Premier League last season than Iraola, whose Bournemouth team were held a remarkable 18 times. It was a league high by a comfortable distance. Leeds in second had 14. Ten came at the Vitality, 52.63% of their home league fixtures, and Bournemouth ultimately missed out on the fifth and final Champions League spot by three points from a Liverpool team that stumbled over the line under Arne Slot.

Over the course of his last 38 league games, Iraola has drawn 21 times. That is a joint record in the Premier League alongside Mark Hughes, whose identical run across 38 games came with Manchester City and Fulham between October 2009 and February 2011. Hughes had a seven-month break between those two jobs, however, making Iraola the first Premier League coach to draw 21 of 38 matches in a continuous sequence.

The sample size at Liverpool is too small for conclusions, admittedly. Iraola is also still searching for balance and assessing his options, as changes in both full-back positions and central midfield have demonstrated regularly. But the 44-year-old knows full well that a draw with Liverpool is far more damaging to his current employer’s aspirations than his previous one. Three from four league games so far have enabled Arsenal and Manchester City to quickly establish an ominous six-point gap over the 2025 champions. The audible groans that greeted the home draws against Nottingham Forest and Fulham confirmed Anfield’s patience has not recovered from last season’s travails.

“That’s totally fair,” Iraola said of the contrasting reactions to a draw at Liverpool and Bournemouth. “But it’s something that I knew before coming here. When you draw 2-2 at Newcastle with Bournemouth it is probably a good result, but I understand that with Liverpool it is not a good result. The goals of the team are different and the expectations are different as well.”

Fulham was a step backwards, according to Iraola, after two steps forward against Ipswich and Atlético Madrid. A younger, fresher Liverpool team restored momentum with Tuesday’s Carabao Cup win over Tottenham. Elements of that performance were as timely for Iraola as the result. Having demanded greater effort from his forward line following the Fulham draw – and then rested Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz against Spurs – youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell, Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni all made tireless contributions to the cup win in their absences.

View image in fullscreen Rio Ngumoha, in action against Atlético Madrid, has has shown his quality as one of Liverpool’s rising stars. Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Academy players appeared more attuned to Iraola’s methods and instructions than their expensive elders. With Liverpool’s midfield balance also under scrutiny and Wirtz following a good Champions League performance with an indifferent Premier League display, as was often the case last season, Iraola may spend the extended international break wrestling with some big calls depending on how his Bournemouth return unfolds. He has shown himself unafraid of making them.

“For me the demands on the players and positions are the same,” Iraola insisted on Friday. “I don’t give different instructions to one player because he is more expensive than another player who has cost us less money. The demands are always the same. But I also have to adjust to the things that some players can do and others cannot do.

“The strengths and weaknesses of players are different, so we have to always adapt the team to try and maximise the collective side of this. In Bournemouth we had players who could run forever and other players who could not do it. It was not like everyone in Bournemouth was running. Some of them were faster, others were slower, some of them scored more goals, some are good at set pieces. There is no standard player. I feel all the players here are doing everything to try to win and to try and get where we want as quickly as possible. But sometimes I need to adapt too to the players that we have.”

Iraola was asked if he would love 11 players with the mentality of Koumas. “That is a cheating question,” he said, laughing. “I love the desire of Koumas, I love what he gives, but every player has different weaknesses and strengths. He is a good example especially for the players coming from the academy, he is grabbing his opportunity and doing everything to try to gain minutes. But I also have to work with Koumas a lot in other areas. There are things he has to improve.”

Everyone at Liverpool, it seems, is learning on a job that demands the finished article.

Sports.title: ‘Embrace the chaos’: Tuchel aims to harness England’s football culture
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has admitted there are times when he craves greater control in matches. But the England head coach feels the more chaotic, adrenaline-fuelled nature of the Premier League will remain his template as he targets glory at Euro 2028.

Tuchel described his team as “maybe not the most economical to play football” in terms of their habit of constantly playing at full throttle. They lost to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final in July when they had nothing left in the tank and watched the game slip away after going 1-0 up in the 55th minute. England barely touched the ball thereafter, had no control and were reeled in, Argentina winning with two late goals.

Tuchel said he would like it if his team “became for 10 minutes more like Spain” when the pressure was on – a reference to the ability of the world champions to dominate the ball; their comfort on it. Ultimately, though, Tuchel will always play to the strengths of his players, what they are used to, what they have grown up with – even what the fans in England most like.

It may be an internal battle for him because he is a coach who finds a lack of control “hard to digest”. But as Tuchel looked ahead to the next international cycle and the Nations League games against Spain (home), Czechia (home and away) and Croatia (away), he talked of how he wanted to “embrace the chaos”.

“I’m just wrestling with myself,” he said. “Even if you control matches in the Premier League, how many English players are there in these teams that really try to control matches? Is this in our DNA? Do we really value control? Is this something that comes easy to us? Or do we go: ‘Yeah, but we’re stuck in midfield, we should go, we should attack.’

“I’ve seen [England] training sessions on the very highest level of my career … with a lot of speed and ball speed, physicality, dribbling. So it makes me just struggle … how and when [to seek control]. Because we’re talking about the highest-pressure moments, the semi-final against Argentina, 80% of the stadium is Argentinian. So now can you please become Spain for 15 minutes …”

View image in fullscreen ‘Do we really value control?’ Thomas Tuchel believes England must play to their attacking strengths. Photograph: Paul Childs/Reuters

Tuchel was asked whether his team’s attempt to dig in grimly and preserve the 1-0 lead against Argentina was a result of their lack of control. “I would say yes,” he replied. “But I would still say it [controlling football] is not how English fans cherish a match. I don’t think that an English supporter goes to a Premier League match and wants to see a controlled match and 1-0 late on. OK, win always. But it comes with international players playing for the teams that are more open to that.

Quick Guide England's squad Show Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford, James Trafford, Jason Steele. Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarrod Branthwaite, Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Guéhi, Lewis Hall, Ezri Konsa, Tino Livramento, Nico O’Reilly, Jarell Quansah. Midfielders: Elliot Anderson, Jude Bellingham, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Alex Scott. Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Eberechi Eze, Anthony Gordon, Harry Kane, Rio Ngumoha, Marcus Rashford, Morgan Rogers, Bukayo Saka. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Deep down, in the core, English players and the spectators – and this is a beautiful thing – they go for it. They say: ‘Let’s play [for] 6-3 or 4-3. Let’s not play 1-0. We want to put the ball up front.’ There was the famous kick-and-rush in earlier times. There is no heritage of: ‘Oh, let’s control around the middle line. Let’s do a deep buildup and then bring them out.’ It’s just like: ‘Come on. Let’s kick the ball into the opponent’s box and fight with them.’

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Now that I have a tournament as an experience, I feel that this team is ready to fight, is always ready to go. This is the beauty of it. That come the high-pressure moments where we can play better football, where we maybe lack even a little bit of courage or this energy … maybe it’s more going down that route.”

It was put to Tuchel that he ought to be able to finesse his gameplan to include spells where the team could retain the ball against elite-level opposition because England have polished players. He said he did not “have the time to coach them” like this. The way Tuchel sees it, he has come into a specific football culture. It is not on him to change it, rather to work with what he has – including the numerous positive traits. Tuchel is not about to push a different game model. “No,” he said. “I know I don’t [do that]. I think it will not suit the characteristics of our players.”

Tuchel said he had “mixed” feelings about the World Cup because of the Argentina defeat. He also accepted that his team could have played better across the piece. But he will not allow the second half against Argentina to override the positives and how, after the win over France in the third-place playoff, it added up to England’s best tournament finish since 1966.

“I have never said it was a big success,” Tuchel said. “I said there were a lot of positives. It was unfulfilled. But why is the expectation so high? When did we last win it? When did we ever win it? Why is the expectation so high that even bringing home a [bronze] medal cannot be acknowledged?”

Sports.title: Manchester City scramble to dramatic WSL win over Liverpool with two goals in added time
Sports.content:
Manchester City continued their winning start to the new Women’s Super League season but the defending champions needed a 90th-minute own goal from Grace Fisk to help them edge past an ever-improving Liverpool side after an entertaining game in which Lauren Hemp scored twice.

Fisk inadvertently turned Grace Clinton’s dangerous cross into her own net to put City 3-2 up and then – with Liverpool searching for an equaliser and committing players forward deep in stoppage time – Hemp added another on the counterattack to make it 4-2 and widen the margin of victory, but that slightly masked how well the visitors had played.

Gareth Taylor – against his former side – will have taken significant encouragement from his Liverpool team’s performance, on a night when they made the league leaders dig deep.

“Playing that way, we believe we’ll win a lot of games this season,” Taylor told Sky Sports, as he praised his team’s effort. “What you saw was a more improved version of what we were towards the end of last season.”

That certainly seemed the case. Nevertheless, the result ensured that City, who had already been the only WSL side who held a 100% winning record after the opening two rounds of games and now will certainly stay top of the table for at least another week, have still not dropped any points in home league fixtures since Andrée Jeglertz took charge in the summer of 2025.

It had looked as though Jeglertz’s City were set for a routine evening when Hemp met Carlotta Wamser’s incisive inside ball and sent a controlled, low finish into the far bottom corner. It was Hemp’s first goal since scoring for England in a victory over Spain in April, her first club goal since scoring in the FA Cup in February and her first WSL goal since last November’s Manchester derby.

Moments after Hemp’s opening goal, with 13 minutes on the clock, the entire crowd rose to applaud the late Matt Beard, the former Liverpool manager, in reference to the year 2013, when he won the first of two consecutive WSL titles with Liverpool.

Supporters of clubs across the WSL and WSL2 have been invited to applaud at the same time in games across this weekend, to mark a year since Beard’s death on 20 September 2025. He was a much-loved character and hugely successful coach at Liverpool, whose performance – particularly in the remainder of the first half – would have done him proud.

View image in fullscreen Vivien Endemann puts Liverpool 2-1 up against Manchester City. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

The away side deservedly struck back and found themselves 2-1 up before the half-hour mark, as their pressing gave the defending champions a headache. First a misunderstanding between Wamser and Alex Greenwood allowed Vivien Endemann to set up Alice Bergström for the equaliser, which she calmly tucked past Ayaka Yamashita.

Soon afterwards, after City failed to clear a cross, Endemann – who had opened her Liverpool account with a debut goal at Charlton on the opening weekend – fired in a shot that Yamashita got a hand to but could only help into the net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Khadija Shaw struck a post from a difficult angle after rounding Khiara Keating, but Shaw eventually did equalise after a goalkeeping error shortly before half-time. Keating – returning to face her former club after her summer move to Liverpool – did well to block Hemp’s strike but was unable to prevent the ball trickling into the path of the onrushing Shaw, who gratefully poked home.

Keating impressed in the second half with a fine reaction save, keeping out a Shaw effort that had looked destined for the top corner at her near post. But the hosts began to build pressure and the introduction of the lively Clinton inside the final 15 minutes boosted their attacking threat.

Her near-post cross proved too difficult for Fisk to clear and – just as they did on countless occasions last term – City lived up to Jeglertz’s mantra of “we will find a way to win”, a message that has been imprinted on the walls of their training base.

Jeglertz hinted at that again as he told Sky Sports: “I’m very pleased with the mentality of the group. They never stop believing, they keep on going and – in the end – we are winners.”

Sports.title: Premier League news: Carrick brushes aside questions over future, Arteta salutes ‘extraordinary’ Dowman
Sports.content:
1. Carrick insists: ‘It’s not a blame game’ Michael Carrick says it will take more than one or two defeats before he comes under internal pressure as the Manchester United head coach. United lost 3-2 to Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, having led 2-0 at Old Trafford. That followed Sunday’s 1-0 home loss to 10-man Manchester City. United also went down 2-0 at Hull on the opening day of the season and conceded a late equaliser at Everton at the beginning of the month. The results have caused Carrick to come under scrutiny and he was reminded before Sunday’s visit to Fulham that his predecessors, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, were sacked after 30 months and 14 months, respectively, in the job. “It will be a lot longer than one or two games of results [before he is under pressure from United’s hierarchy],” Carrick said: “It’s irrelevant for me. I know the club, I know the role, I know what’s expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard. “In terms of the future and ownership and how long I’ve got, it’s totally nothing, it’s ridiculous to think that way in the position I’m in: it’s just not on the radar. It’s two or three games we haven’t had certain results. We’ve got to perform and we’ve got a lot of games to plan for.” Carrick is content to take ownership of his team’s performance. “That’s why I’m here. It’s my responsibility, I’m fine with that,” he said. “It’s not a blame game. We always search for things to look at and find the blame, sometimes it gets too much. Blame me, it’s no problem, but it’s not about blaming people. It’s about finding solutions. It’s a collective thing. I know where we want to go and we want to get there fast. We don’t like losing matches, but it doesn’t affect what we do next.” The 45-year-old was asked if he needs to show more emotion on the touchline. “I need to show more emotion? In what way?” he replied. “What do you want me to show?” On Friday JJ Gabriel travelled to Barcelona for discussions regarding potentially joining the club, with United understood to have found out via the media despite the 15-year-old being registered with them. On Tuesday Gabriel told United he wanted his registration rescinded because he wishes to join another club. Real Madrid have a firm interest and it is understood Gabriel and his advisers travelled for preliminary talks with Barcelona. Carrick said: “The situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's OK is the important thing." Jamie Jackson

2. Dowman takes step up in his stride Mikel Arteta has praised Max Dowman’s “extraordinary” transition from schoolboy to Arsenal first-team squad member and backed the teenager to make more of an impact this season. Dowman became the first 16-year-old since Wayne Rooney in October 2002 to score twice for a Premier League club in Arsenal’s victory over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday, after bursting on to the scene last year. That was his first appearance of the campaign, having been an unused substitute on four occasions as Arsenal have won all seven of their fixtures.



Dowman, who has been training with Arsenal’s first team since he was 14, completed his GCSEs in the summer and he will study for a BTec qualification after deciding against taking A-Levels. Arteta said Dowman’s development was still being carefully managed by Arsenal after a couple of years of having to balance his studies. “It’s not easy,” said the Arsenal manager. “That’s what tells you about the craziness of the age and the environment he still lives in with the demands and the competition he needs to face during the week. But the way he has handled it, him and the family, it has been extraordinary. If he is here, he has to be here in all conditions and we cannot treat him differently in many aspects.” Dowman is in contention to be on the bench to face Brighton on Saturday as Arsenal attempt to make it eight successive victories to start the season for the first time since 1903. Arteta is convinced more opportunities will come his way sooner rather than later.

“That’s the best way to knock on the door: to do it on the pitch, not in the office,” he said. “What Max did the other day, alongside all the players as well, that haven’t played that many minutes, it was really impressive.” View image in fullscreen Arsenal’s Max Dowman turns 17 in January when he could go out on loan. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/Shutterstock Premier League regulations do not allow players under 17 to be sent out on loan but Luton are understood to have registered an interest in Dowman, who was coached by their manager, Jack Wilshere, when he played for Arsenal’s under-18s. Arteta said it was possible Dowman could be allowed to leave in January, by which point he will be 17, but that his immediate future was at Arsenal. “We haven’t really listened to any of the possibilities because we were crystal clear that we wanted to have him in the squad, that we wanted him to be part of the pre-season and then start to see where we are from there,” Arteta said. “We will evaluate every six months, where we are and what is the best thing for him to do and then make the right decision. It depends on a lot of factors – what he needs and what the team needs as well, the availability we have in the squad, the minutes that he is playing and the qualities of those minutes. We have to be open but now the focus is to be here and to impact the team.” Ed Aarons

3. De Zerbi grants Tonali time to settle Roberto De Zerbi insists Sandro Tonali is not feeling the pressure of his price tag despite a mixed start to life at Tottenham. The midfielder became the most expensive player in the club’s history when he joined from Newcastle for £92.5m in the summer. De Zerbi made a big play to sign Tonali amid interest from Manchester City and Arsenal, delivering a two-hour sales pitch to his fellow Italian to convince him to move to north London. He outlined how central Tonali would be to his plans and explained what he could expect from Spurs’ fans and the team’s style of football. Tonali has started all four Premier League games this season – in which Spurs have drawn twice and lost twice without scoring – but has produced underwhelming defensive numbers and created only three chances. De Zerbi revealed he had spoken to the 26-year-old about the weight of the price tag and claimed the player “doesn’t feel the pressure about that”. The Spurs manager pointed out that Tonali took time to adapt in his first season at Milan in 2020 before becoming one of the most sought-after young midfielders in the world once he settled there. De Zerbi said “the adaptation has been not so fast” at Tottenham “but it can happen”, adding: “It is not so easy to change city, to change everything, for the players. Sometimes the adaptation is immediate, sometimes you need more time.” View image in fullscreen Sandro Tonali has started all four Premier League games this season, but Spurs are still seeking their first win. Photograph: Chloe Knott/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock Tottenham’s struggles in front of goal have not been helped by Tonali’s inability to create chances for the forwards. The goalless draw against Everton was the first in 140 games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and following a 0-0 against Nottingham Forest, equalling Spurs’ tally of goalless games in the previous 181 matches. The last time they recorded three or more consecutive goalless draws in the league was 25 years ago under George Graham, when they went to four. It is a remarkable run, especially after a summer spend of more than £300m, that leaves Spurs in 17th going into Saturday’s game against Aston Villa, who have also struggled after a summer of major change. De Zerbi maintained he is happy with Tonali’s performances – even though he believes they can improve – and described him as “a complete midfielder”. “His physical characteristics are to play box to box but he started his career as a playmaker. He’s good enough with the ball, he’s good enough without the ball.” Sam Cunningham

Sports.title: I’m 44 and Man United will not win another Premier League title in my lifetime
Sports.content:
I’m 44 and Man United will not win another Premier League title in my lifetime

Manchester United fans have been dealt a brutal reality check.

In a season that initially offered so much hope, the same challenges have once again emerged without warning.

5 Manchester United have made another underwhelming start to the season Credit: Getty



Two home defeats in the space of four days did little to enthuse supporters who may otherwise have fallen into a false state of security following the 4-0 Champions League destruction of Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah.

Last weekend’s controversial 1-0 defeat to ten-man Manchester City left United in 13th place and already eight-points off the top.

Their cataclysmic collapse in midweek, throwing away a two-goal lead before being dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton, felt like the needle mover.

Not because United fans haven’t become accustomed to the inexplicable over the last decade, but instead due to the same mistakes being repeated.



Millions invested in the team, a plethora of managers all hoping they can be the one to turn the Old Trafford tide, but ultimately, the same end result.

Boss Michael Carrick, a man who contributed to the club’s glory days, is now firmly in the firing line while fans have again slipped to a low ebb.



For talkSPORT’s chief football correspondent Alex Crook, the chances of the Red Devils lifting another Premier League title are minuscule, regardless of who is in the dugout.

The Manchester United fan provided his sobering reality on the latest episode of talkSPORT’s Fiery Fridays podcast.



The glory days are over...

"So the realisation for me and my hot take this week, I'm 44 now, probably not going to live until I'm 100, realistically,” Crook began.

"Even if I did, I don't think United are going to win the title in my lifetime, I don't think it's going to happen.

5 United's last league title came in 2013 and they have come nowhere close to repeating the feat ever since Credit: Getty

"My big wish now, I've been there and seen it, I've had the glory days, I want us to win something significant so I can share the moment with my two lads who I've forced into following in my footsteps.



"But I don't think that's a realistic ambition anymore, I just think they're so far behind.

"All the time the players are in situ and INEOS and Sir Jim Ratcliffe come in and make the situation worse in my opinion, and not better.

"They've put people like Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada in positions that their CVs don't really warrant.

“They've destroyed the morale of the football club, the fans hate INEOS and Ratcliffe as much as they despise the Glazers.”



Asked how the 20-time top-flight champions return to competing for Premier League titles and the Champions League, Crook provided fans with a huge dose of reality.

5 Man United fan Crook has resigned himself to eternal Premier League failure

"We're going to have to cherish that win over Sabah because we played a pub team,” he added.

"We're not going to play anybody else as bad as that for the rest of the season and I fear we're not going to get out of the Champions League, League phase.



"How embarrassing would that be if we ended up getting knocked out and not even qualifying for the extra round at the end of it?

'The club is broken'

"I'm just really down about the club, it's completely broken to me, I know it was 26 years between titles last time around, it has been 13 already, so we're halfway there.

"I'm not sure there's a genius in the surrounding areas who's going to come in and save us.

“There's not an Eric Cantona coming over the hills to completely rewrite the history of this football club.



5 The rot has long set in at Old Trafford and Crook believes minority owners INEOS are not helping the cause Credit: Getty

"And actually, only three men [managers] have ever won the league title at Manchester United, I don't think there's going to be a fourth."

Voice of talkSPORT Adrian Durham concurred with his broadcast colleague’s desperate monologue.

He quipped: "I think you are going to live forever, Crooky, to be honest with you, the way you live your life and there's no consequences, you are going to live forever.



"So, Man United are never going to win the league again, I cannot see that happening any time soon and even after that, you've got to rebuild a squad, others will be growing at the same time

"The scary thing about it is, Arsenal are incredibly well run, it's incredibly stable, they've got about three players for every position, and I don't even think Man City are going to get that close to them this season, even though they've started well.

"So, yes, Man United are absolutely miles off it, I make you absolutely right."

5 Man United's last trophy came in the 2024 FA Cup final Credit: Getty



Having the final say, United fan Angelina Kelly then joked: "We don't know how long Crook will live, I was trying to give him at least another 40 years for argument's sake

"United had to wait 41 years before, so maybe it'll be similar, who knows?

"But I agree as well, the ownership's lack of ambition is clearly the problem and they're never going to turn things around if they don't actually sort out the root of the issues."

Manchester United head to Fulham on Sunday needing a win to get their domestic campaign back on track.



Following the three-week international break, a crucial run of fixtures await Carrick's side.

United face key clashes with Tottenham, Leeds and Chelsea, with trips to Atletico Madrid and Como up next in the Champions League.

Sports.title: Chelsea told they’re ‘definitely not’ title contenders as Xabi Alonso sets unwanted record
Sports.content:
Chelsea are not going to be in the Premier League title race this season - there is so much wrong with the 'crazy club'.

Those are the thoughts of Adrian Durham, who watched on as the Blues were beaten 3-0 by Brentford on Friday night.



3 Chelsea were easily beaten by Brentford on Friday, losing away to the Bees in the Premier League for the first time Credit: Getty

Keith Andrews outclassed Xabi Alonso at the Gtech Community Stadium as his side moved up to third in the table.

Meanwhile, Chelsea dropped down to seventh after being handed their second loss of the season in just five games.

The teams went in goalless at half time, but Brentford came out the much better side in the second half, opening the scoring just after the hour mark through Jaidon Anthony.



Igor Thiago then made it two with nine minutes to go and ex-Liverpool man Fabio Carvalho added the third in stoppage time.

The impressive result handed the Bees their first-ever Premier League home victory over Chelsea.



They were winless in five meetings beforehand, but now Xabi Alonso is the first Blues manager to lose on the road against them.

Chelsea out of the Premier League title race

A 3-0 loss for Chelsea has them sitting on seven points after five games and already five points off the top of the table.



That could increase to eight if Arsenal or Manchester City win their matches across the upcoming weekend of action.

And talkSPORT's Durham has already ruled them out of challenging for the Premier League title this campaign.

Speaking after the full-time whistle, he said: "So many questions about this Chelsea performance...fundamentally, they are definitely not Premier League title contenders, we can see that.

3 Alonso has lost two of his opening five league games as Chelsea boss Credit: AFP



"I think there's so much wrong with them."

Arsenal legend Martin Keown added: "It's extremely disappointing from a Chelsea point of view, we were never really convinced.

"The wealth that the club has and the players they buy, but then you see that tonight...it wasn't particularly convincing."

He later continued: "That is a wake-up call for Chelsea."

And Durham then concluded: "They're a crazy club, Chelsea. They started with a 36-year-old in midfield and finished with a 16-year-old in midfield. That's how crazy they are."

Jordan Henderson, formerly of Brentford, made his first start for Chelsea before academy prospect Madhi Nicoll-Jazuli was brought on to join him for the final stages of the match.



3 Brentford outclassed Chelsea to leave the Blues well off the pace in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Jason Cundy's comments come back to bite him

Chelsea superfan Jason Cundy would have been watching their defeat to Brentford behind his hands on Friday.

Not only because of the poor performance, but because just before the season started, he predicted the Blues to win the title.

“I’m going to make a statement now. There is no reason why Chelsea cannot win this title. In fact, I’m going to say it. Chelsea will win the title," Cundy said at the start of August.



“There is something about Chelsea. We have got a cheat code. I’m not proud of it, but we can win the title for a number of reasons.

“Have you seen our front three? Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer - Palmer’s had a rest, Joao Pedro’s had a rest.

“Our midfield, the recruitment at the back. It almost certainly looks like we could be playing three at the back with someone in Xabi Alonso, who knows how to win a title.

“One game a week, we saw how beneficial that could be when Antonio Conte came in, went to three at the back. Win the title. History is going to repeat itself."



But after losing in such a fashion, it seems Cundy's title shout may have been a little bit too ambitious.

And Jamie O'Hara has made sure to rub it in, posting an edited image of Cundy dressed as a bee and writing: 'Up the Bees'.
