The attacks on Saudi oil assets have directly impacted global energy markets and the price of petrol and diesel in many countries has sharply risen in recent weeks, compounding already elevated costs caused by the blockades of the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the country's de facto ruler, has personally asked US President Donald Trump to take military action against the Houthis, two sources familiar with the matter told CBS News, the BBC's US media partner.

Trump has so far declined to involve the US military directly, offering instead to assist with intelligence and targeting support, the sources said.

A senior Trump administration official told the BBC: "We are in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Yemen government regarding regional stability."

Earlier this week, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said the Houthis had launched drones and missiles at Saudi Arabia in retaliation for more than 450 Saudi air strikes on their territory over the past week.

The United Nations Security Council held an emergency meeting on Tuesday, during which both Yemen's government and Saudi Arabia called for more decisive action against the Houthis, who they accused of choking the Bab al-Mandab Strait as a way of applying economic pressure.

Council members agreed that freedom of navigation in the Red Sea must be maintained to prevent disruption to global supply chains.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

The fighting has reportedly left more than 150,000 people dead and triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with more than 22 million people in need of some form of aid, according to the UN.

Additional reporting by Tabby Wilson.

World.title: Court overturns judgement ordering NDC’s deregistration
World.content:
The Court of Appeal in Abuja has set aside the earlier judgement of the Federal High Court, Lokoja which ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to deregister the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) as a political party.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the Federal High Court in Lokoja, Kogi State, in June, set aside its earlier judgement directing INEC to register NDC as a political party.

The ruling followed an application by the Peace Movement Party (PMP), which asked that the December 2025 judgement be set aside because it was not joined in the suit.

The judge, Isah Dashen, upheld the PMP application and ruled that all relevant parties must be heard before any substantive decision can be made in the matter.

The judge then declared that such an omission rendered the entire process null and void and ruled that the status quo be restored to its state before the December 2025 judgement, pending the determination of the substantive suit.

The NDC subsequently appealed the judgement.

Judgement overturned

In its judgement on Friday, the Court of Appeal in Abuja set aside the judgement of the lower court which ordered INEC to deregister the NDC.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The National Leader of the NDC, Seriake Dickson, announced this in a post on his X handle on Friday.

Mr Dickson, a serving senator, said the judgement was delivered by Justice Mohammed Danjuma and read by Justice Sule Hassan.

“We want to use this opportunity once again to commend the Nigerian judiciary, and in particular, Hon. Justice Danjuma and Hon. Justice Hassan, for upholding the integrity of the Nigerian judiciary and, by their decisions, expanding the sphere of multiparty democratic participation in Nigeria,” he said.

‘Unexpected assault’

The national leader described the initial ruling by Mr Dashen of the federal high court as an “unexpected assault on our constitutional right to participate and an attempt to narrow the democratic space.”

“Happily, today, by the decision of the Court of Appeal, the Nigerian democratic space has been protected, and the NDC’s right to participate in all political activities as a registered political party has been upheld,” he said.

Mr Dickson recalled that the NDC leaders were “bombarded with several calls” for sympathy, support and prayers when the initial ruling was delivered.

“Today, our collective prayers have been answered.

“The NDC continues to exist. Our registration remains valid and subsisting, and we and all our candidates will participate in all elections in 2027 and beyond, by the grace of God,” he stated.

“With this conviction, we look forward to the forthcoming elections and are confident that the NDC will emerge victorious at the polls, by the grace of God.”

World.title: FG deploys experts to assist in probe of deaths of 37 detained illegal mining suspects in Niger
World.content:
The Federal Government has sent a team of mining and technical experts to Niger State to assist in the investigation of the deaths of 37 illegal mining suspects in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna.

The development comes amid widening investigations into the deaths, with the Niger State Government, NSCDC, Nigeria Police Force and other relevant agencies conducting separate inquiries into the incident.

The Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development said the experts were deployed to establish the facts surrounding the incident and determine whether activities at the mining sites or other factors contributed to the deaths.

The permanent secretary of the ministry, Faruk Yabo, who led a federal government delegation to Niger State on behalf of the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, disclosed this during a visit to Governor Mohammed Bago and families of the deceased.

Mr Yabo said the team would conduct a detailed investigation covering the circumstances before, during and after the detention of the victims.

He said the investigation would produce a report on what happened to the deceased.

Mr Yabo described the incident as tragic and unacceptable, stressing that mining activities should contribute to the welfare and development of Nigerians rather than result in loss of lives.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I extend the deepest condolences of the minister and ministry to the governor, his cabinet, and the people, especially the families of the victims of this highly tragic incident,” he said.

“This is totally an unacceptable situation. Mining should be for the good of all and not a basis to lose lives.”

Cause of deaths yet to be established

Receiving the federal delegation, Governor Bago said it was too early to reach a definitive conclusion on the cause of the deaths.

He, however, said investigators were examining possible suffocation arising from overcrowding, as well as exposure to hazardous substances associated with mining activities.

The governor said the state government had ordered forensic and medical examinations, including autopsies, to establish the scientific cause of the deaths.

The deaths have prompted investigations by multiple government and security agencies, with authorities seeking to establish the circumstances surrounding the miners’ deaths while they were in NSCDC custody.

NSCDC officials suspended

Meanwhile, the NSCDC Commandant in Niger State, Suberu Aniviye, and members of his team have been suspended to allow for an unhindered investigation into the incident.

The NSCDC national leadership has also constituted a high-powered panel to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

The panel is expected to examine the condition of the detainees at the time of their arrest, their period in custody, the conditions under which they were detained and the medical attention provided to them.

The incident has generated public concern and protests in parts of Minna, prompting authorities to appeal for calm and urge residents not to take the law into their own hands.

Niger suspends mining activities

Governor Bago has also announced the suspension of mining activities across Niger State pending the outcome of the investigations.

The governor said the incident should serve as a wake-up call to stakeholders in the mining sector on the need to strengthen regulation and ensure that the protection of human lives remains central to efforts to tackle illegal mining.

He said the state government would continue to cooperate with federal agencies and other relevant authorities to establish the facts surrounding the deaths and ensure appropriate action based on the findings.

World.title: Gunmen kill three, injure many in Plateau market attack
World.content:
Gunmen on Friday night attacked a vegetable market in Mangu town in the Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State, killing three people and injuring several others.

The President of the Mwaghavul Development Association (MDA), Bulus Dabit, said the attackers opened fire on a vehicle leaving the market at about 8 p.m., killing two women and a young man.

The attack occurred as traders and buyers were preparing to close for the day, triggering panic and forcing people to flee in different directions.

Many people were reportedly injured in the ensuing stampede.

Mr Dabit said the identities of the three victims were not immediately known, adding that those seriously injured were referred to the Jos University Teaching Hospital (JUTH).

“At about 8 p.m. on Friday, gunmen shot several times at a vehicle leaving the vegetable market in Mangu, killing two women and a young man,” he said.

Another source, John Haruna, said the sudden gunfire caused panic at the market, with people running in different directions in an attempt to escape.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Dabit condemned the attack.

“Security agencies must leverage intelligence and technology to apprehend the perpetrators of these dastardly acts, as they would not be far from the scene of the crime,” he said.

The attack came hours after the MDA raised concerns over continued threats to communities in Mangu.

In a statement signed by its Director of Public Affairs, Friday Derwam, following a joint meeting of the association’s national executive, women’s leadership and youth leadership, the association called for an immediate investigation into recent killings in the local government area.

READ ALSO: Four killed in fresh Plateau attacks

The group also claimed that more than 750 Mwaghavul people had been killed in attacks since 2023.

The latest attack adds to the security concerns in Mangu, which has witnessed repeated attacks and communal violence in recent years.

As of the time of filing this report, the police had not issued an official statement on the incident.

World.title: 30 children rescued from illegal orphanage in Kwara
World.content:
Thirty children have been rescued from an illegal orphanage in Ilorin, Kwara State.

The state government said the children, found at Iranlowo Oluwa Orphanage and Children’s Home in the state capital, are undergoing post-rescue assessment and rehabilitation after their rescue.

They were rescued by the state Ministry of Social Development after community members raised concerns about the living conditions of the children at the facility.

The children, comprising boys and girls of between ages two and 15, have been relocated to a facility under the supervision of the ministry.

Speaking on Friday, the Commissioner for Social Development, Mariam Imam, said the intervention involved assessing their immediate needs, as well as their health and educational conditions.

Mrs Imam said the ministry was also working on family tracing and reunification, where appropriate.

She added that those who cannot be reunited with their families would be considered for placement in approved care facilities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The commissioner further directed that all orphanages, children’s homes and other child-care institutions operating in Kwara State must register with the ministry.

READ ALSO: NAPTIP uncovers trafficking network using orphanage to sell children

The Director of Social Work at the ministry, Hamzat Abdulfatah, who was involved in the rescue operation, said the intervention had further strengthened collaboration among relevant stakeholders.

“We now understand that if we manage this process properly and follow due process, these children will have the opportunity to live better and more fulfilled lives.”

World.title: APC challenges Atiku to present alternatives to Tinubu reforms
World.content:
The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Felix Morka, has challenged former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to present detailed alternatives to the economic reforms of President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

Mr Morka said criticism of the government’s policies was not enough, arguing that Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), should tell Nigerians how he intends to address the country’s economic problems and improve their living standards.

The APC spokesperson spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday while responding to criticism of the Tinubu administration’s handling of the economy.

“You know, he should be telling Nigerians exactly what he plans to do to improve the lives of Nigerians,” Mr Morka said, adding Atiku had yet to present a detailed policy alternative to the measures introduced by the Tinubu administration.

Mr Morka particularly defended the removal of the petrol subsidy, saying all the major presidential candidates in the 2023 election had supported its removal.

“All of those who ran in that election were unanimous in their promise to Nigerians to remove fuel subsidies. This president did that,” he said.

The APC spokesperson acknowledged that Nigerians were experiencing hardship but argued that the reforms were necessary to address structural problems that had accumulated over several years.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our country was broke. So when you say things are hard today because we had to take some correctional measures to fix problems that have been there for decades,” he said.

Mr Morka also rejected the argument that the reforms had worsened the country’s economic position, saying the economy was now on a stronger footing than when Mr Tinubu assumed office.

“The country, the economy is today by far better, standing on stronger footing than it did when this president came along,” he said.

Cost of Atiku’s proposals

The APC publicist also questioned how Atiku would finance any proposal to restore or expand subsidies.

He argued that promises to reduce the cost of petrol, electricity or other essential services would have financial implications and should be accompanied by a clear funding plan.

“Any promise you make, there’s a cost to it,” Mr Morka said.

His comments come amid Atiku’s criticism of the government’s economic policies and calls for measures to reduce the burden of rising living costs.

Morka defends naira reforms

Mr Morka also defended the government’s foreign exchange reforms, particularly the harmonisation of exchange rates.

He argued that the previous system did not accurately reflect the value of the naira and said the government’s decision to harmonise the rates was necessary to improve the country’s economic prospects.

“When the government harmonised the exchange rates, that was necessary from an economic point of view to give Nigeria a fighting chance of economic recovery,” he said.

Mr Morka said the administration should be assessed against the economic conditions it inherited, insisting that its reforms were beginning to improve the country’s macroeconomic position.

“The average Nigerian understands that without the policies of this government, we won’t even have a country,” he said.

He also dismissed comparisons between Atiku and Mr Tinubu, pointing to what he described as the president’s record in office.

“Comparing Atiku Abubakar with the president who has a record, as we speak, demonstrable record of transforming the economy of this country, I think that’s a ridiculous comparison,” Mr Morka said.

World.title: Medical expert identifies major cause of sudden deaths in Nigeria, other countries
World.content:
A professor of haematology, Theresa Nwagha, has said that blood clots also known as Venous Thromboembolism (VTE), remain the major cause of sudden deaths globally.

Ms Nwagha stated this on Thursday in Enugu while delivering the 252nd Inaugural Lecture of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), with the topic: “The Balance of Blood Fluidity: From Bleeding to Clotting in Health and Disease”.

She explained that VTE occurs when blood clots form in the veins and block normal blood flow, revealing that about 10 million cases of blood clots occur globally each year, resulting in about two million deaths.

The blood specialist said blood clots could affect both sick and apparently healthy people, sometimes leading to sudden death.

According to her, 25 per cent of the time, there are no symptoms concerning blood clots.

The professor of haematology and coagulation medicine listed the VTE risk factors to include prolonged sitting, obesity, stress and long-distance journeys lasting more than four hours.

She stressed the need to always assess the risk of thrombosis or blood clots to prevent sudden deaths popularly known as “Fall and Die”.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She explained that sitting for long periods, especially while working on computers, could cause blood to remain stagnant in the lower legs, increasing the risk of clot formation.

She added that blood clots could sometimes be mistaken for muscle injuries, exercise-induced asthma or ordinary fatigue.

The professor called for hospital-wide risk assessment and preventive treatment, known as thromboprophylaxis, to reduce cases of VTE.

She called for the integration of VTE awareness and early identification into primary healthcare.

Factors affecting efforts to improve VTE management

Ms Nwagha said low public awareness, gaps in medical training and the loss of healthcare professionals to migration, popularly known as “Japa syndrome”, have affected efforts to improve VTE management.

She said these challenges contributed to the establishment of the UNTH Anticoagulation Steward Committee by the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH).

“We want to convert anticoagulation from a fearfully understood clinical hazard into a highly disciplined standard life-saving medical act,” she said.

The professor also highlighted the importance of multidisciplinary care for women, particularly during pregnancy and other reproductive health conditions where blood clotting could pose serious risks.

According to her, proper teamwork among healthcare professionals could improve outcomes for women at risk.

“Women on oral contraceptive, IVF, high doses of oesterogene and even athletes are at risk of thrombosis,” she said.

Ms Nwagha further discussed the use of digital health and Artificial Intelligence as tools for improving VTE risk assessment and providing more precise care.

Commendations

Earlier, the UNN Vice-Chancellor, Simon Ortuanya, represented by J.U.J Onwumere, congratulated Ms Nwagha for the inaugural lecture and encouraged her to do more research on haematology and coagulation.

Dignitaries at the event, including former minister of power, Chinedu Nebo, as well as families and friends, commended Ms Nwagha for her immense contributions to safeguarding public health in the country.

(NAN)

World.title: Soludo pardons jailed native doctor, gives him appointment
World.content:
Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State has granted a pardon to a popular native doctor in the state, Chukwudozie Nwangwu.

Mr Nwangwu, popularly known as “Akwa Okuko Tiwaraki,” was arrested in February 2025 and, subsequently sentenced to two years imprisonment in February this year for charges related to preparation of charms for criminals.

The court later ordered that his two year-jail term would include 13 months he had been in prison which reduced the jail term to 11 months.

Like Mr Nwangu, at least seven other native doctors were also arrested and are currently being prosecuted.

Pardon and appointment

Nelson Omenugha, the special adviser to Mr Soludo on Youth Reformation, in a statement on Friday said the governor visited the prison facility in fulfilment of his duties when he made the announcement.

Mr Omenugha also said the governor, further appointed the convict as an ambassador for youth reformation.

“This is the heart of Youth Reformation: not just punishment, but correction, restoration, a new purpose and a new Onye Anambra,” the aide said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Video clip

Meanwhile, Mr Soludo was seen in a viral video clips while on a visit to the prison facility, flanked by top government officials and prison authorities.

In another clip, Mr Soludo was seen asking Mr Nwangwu when his jail term would be due and subsequently informed the native doctor that he would be leaving the facility with him.

Turning to a prison official, the governor said: “I will sign the documents for his release now.”

The clip showed him signing the documents.

“Now, let’s get to work. The work of developing Anambra, we will be doing together,” Mr Soludo told Mr Nwangu in a veiled reference to his appointment.

Background

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the conviction of native doctor followed Governor Soludo’s signing of the Anambra State Homeland Security Bill into law in January 2025.

The law, aside from creating the Agunechemba vigilante group, equally banned the making of charms for the commission of crime and the performing of sacrifices along the road in the state.

It was targeted at native doctors who prepare charms for criminals terrorising residents of the South-eastern state.

The legislation equally outlawed the practice of Oke-Ite and Ezenwanyi for the purpose of wealth accumulation through supernatural means.

“Okite” is an Igbo phrase for a big pot used for ritual practices.

“Ezenwanyi,” on the other hand, is an Igbo phrase for a female spiritualist.

The Anambra State Homeland Security law 2025 also imposes six years imprisonment or N20 million or both on defaulters upon conviction.

The legislation seeks to check growing insecurity in the state.

World.title: INTERVIEW: Why I moved to India-Former Remo Stars Captain, Junior Nduka
World.content:
Former Remo Stars captain and Home-based Super Eagles defender Junior Nduka has explained why he chose to continue his career with Sporting Club Delhi in India after spells in Nigeria and Iraq.

Nduka, who rose through the Remo Stars youth system before captaining the club and helping them win their first NPFL title, recently completed his move to SC Delhi, after a season in the Iraqi League.

In this exclusive interview with PREMIUM TIMES, the defender discusses what attracted him to India, the lessons he picked up in Iraq, his approach to choosing clubs, and why financial considerations are also an important part of life as a professional footballer.

Excerpts…

PT: You have just completed your move to SC Delhi in India. What went through your mind when the opportunity came, and what ultimately convinced you to make this move?

NDUKA JNR: I will say what went through my mind or came into my mind then was what the club is willing to offer because, aside from passion, we ain’t just playing for passion, we’re playing for money.

So that’s why I had to choose to go to Sporting Club Delhi. And aside from choosing money, it’s a good club. When I checked everything I needed to check, that I needed to know about the club, I had to go for it because I know it’s a good club.

It’s a good league, you know. People think all these countries are not footballing countries. No, they are. They play good football, they have the facilities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

So those are the things that came into my mind and made me decide to go to India.

PT: You moved from Remo Stars to Iraq and have now moved to India within a relatively short period. How would you describe this phase of your career and how much has it challenged you as a player and as a person?

NDUKA JNR: Yeah, these leagues you just mentioned, it’s different ballgames in all these leagues. It’s a different ballgame in the Nigerian Premier Football League and the Iraqi Stars League as well.

So the little experience I got from the NPFL, combined with playing on the continent and the national team, I think I was able to make use of it in the Iraqi Stars League.

And now I’m heading to Sporting Club Delhi in India. It’s going to be a different ballgame there because of different teammates, different atmosphere, different weather, different terrain, different tactics, different style of play.

But as a professional, we know how to deal with things like this. And I pray everything goes well.

PT: What did you learn from your time in Iraq, particularly from playing in a completely different football environment, that you believe will help you succeed in India?

NDUKA JNR: Particularly, I would say what I learned from Iraq is adaptation.

You know, you’re going to a different country, playing differently from where you used to play. You just need to adapt quickly into their system, into their style of play, how they play, how they behave and all of these things.

PT: You were reportedly linked with other clubs before settling on SC Delhi. How competitive was the process, and why did you feel this was the right destination for you at this stage of your career?

NDUKA JNR: I would say it’s not competitive. I go for what I want, what I feel like is best for me as a football player.

And I saw so many comments, you know, which is their opinion. It’s not mine. Because they’re not going to feed me tomorrow after playing football.

So I know data is cheap these days. You can buy data of 100 naira or 100 MB and just come and see something and just, you know, write whatever you want and just go offline without considering the player.

So that’s how it is.

Imagine offering, let’s say, $3,000 outside the country and you want someone who’s playing in the NPFL to sit in the NPFL because they are not in a footballing country or because of what people will say and all of these things.

It is what I want. It is what I choose.

PT: SC Delhi are making their mark in the Indian football landscape. What have the club and the coaching staff told you about their expectations of you, and what role do they want you to play?

NDUKA JNR: I spoke with the club’s sporting director alongside the coach, but what we discussed is confidential.

But for me, I am going to help the club because they are a good club. Just like I said earlier, they’re a good team, a team who knows what they want.

You know, it’s just quite unfortunate we got knocked out in the Durand Cup against East Bengal in the semi-final.

So it tells you how prepared this club is and how far they want to go.

PT: You are known as a defender who is comfortable playing out from the back and can also contribute from set pieces. What part of your game are you most determined to bring to the side or improve on during your time in India?

NDUKA JNR: They are a team who are already prepared. I am just going to help, to contribute, you know, to contribute with what I have, with what I’m bringing.

And just like you said, I’m a defender who can play from the back. Aside from playing from the back, I had to help the team to defend at first. Then trying to, and next passes, combine playing from the defence.

If the coach wants me, fine. And if he does not, I just have to maintain my role, my position.

World.title: Real Warri Pikin in dilemma?
World.content:
By Tony-Okafor Favour

Popular comedian Real Warri Pikin cannot deny being in a dilemma after she was forced to apologise to her husband and fans over her viral interaction with singer Timaya during his performance at the 2026 AFRIMMA Awards in Dallas, United States.

The comedienne really did not expect the buzz that greeted her one-night stage appearance with the “Egberi Papa 1 of Bayelsa.” But then, it is what it is.

And Real Warri Pikin is everywhere now, explaining herself and tendering apologies to her husband and fans. In fact, the buzz somehow took the shine off her win on the night. The comedian won Best Stand-Up Comedian at the event, yet nobody is talking about it. Instead, attention has shifted to the controversy sparked by her stage appearance with Timaya.

In a video shared on her Instagram page, she explained that she was backstage while Timaya was performing when he invited a woman to join him on stage.

According to her, she rushed out because she enjoys a good performance and did not know that Timaya’s routine involved bringing a woman on stage and lifting her.

She said she initially resisted when the singer asked her to jump on him, but eventually participated after he urged her not to spoil his performance.The moment, which was entertaining to those present at the event, sparked criticism online after videos surfaced.

World.title: 2027: Ondo APC to set up reconciliation committees
World.content:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

AKURE — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Ondo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) is set to establish nine-member reconciliation committees in each of the 18 local government areas of the state.

Chairman of the APC Reconciliation Committee, Prince Biyi Poroye, disclosed this in Akure during a meeting with local government chairmen and other party stakeholders.

Poroye said the committees would comprise nine members each and would be tasked with deepening reconciliation at the grassroots and addressing grievances among party members.

He said the state reconciliation committee was inaugurated by Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa following disagreements arising from the state and National Assembly primaries in the state.

According to him, the exercise was not only about electoral victory but also aimed at rebuilding unity, discipline and inclusiveness within the party.

“Reconciliation is about changing mindsets. There is nothing to share in losing,” Poroye said.

He said the committee had received complaints, including allegations that the governor was not carrying party members along in appointments.

Poroye said the reconciliation process was intended to discourage attacks and factional tendencies within the party.

“We are shortchanging ourselves if we keep fighting one another. If you contest and the party changes your name, it should not be the end of life. We are appealing to our members that reconciliation is possible,” he said.

The Chief of Staff to the governor, Olusegun Omojuwa, commended Aiyedatiwa for embracing reconciliation, saying taking the process to the grassroots would strengthen the party.

“I want to thank the Governor of Ondo State for believing in peace. This is what can really move our state forward,” Omojuwa said.

He urged party members and leaders to cooperate with the reconciliation committee, saying extending the structure to the local government areas would help deepen the process.

The Chairman of Idanre Local Government, Smart Omotadowa, said grassroots unity was key to the success of the initiative and urged members to support APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

“The best way to make the reconciliation process work is to take it to the grassroots level. There is no way we can have it better than to work in unity,” he said.

Omotadowa urged APC members across the 18 local government areas to support the party’s candidates in the 2027 elections and work together.

A member of the committee, Erelu Mudupola Martins, warned that unresolved grievances could affect the party’s prospects, stressing the need for members to close ranks.

“There is no second in any election. We can’t afford to lose any position to the opposition,” Martins said.

She urged party members to support the reconciliation initiative and ensure that the process reached loyalists at the grassroots.

Martins said the party must “come together and close ranks” ahead of the 2027 elections.

She added that the APC was seeking to improve on its 2023 performance, saying, “We gave Tinubu 68 per cent in 2023; we want to do more than that in 2027.”

World.title: Catholic Bishops demand end to insecurity, poverty
World.content:
By Olayinka Latona

LAGOS — The Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) has called for an end to insecurity, poverty and what it described as bad governance, saying violence, poor infrastructure and economic hardship continue to undermine the wellbeing of Nigerians.

The bishops also outlined measures ahead of the 2027 general elections and declared December 8, 2026, as a special national day of prayer and fasting for the success of the elections.

The bishops made their positions known in a communiqué issued at the end of their Second Plenary Meeting, held at Our Lady and St Kizito Pastoral Centre, Oke-Gada, Ede, Osun State, from September 10 to 18, 2026.

The communiqué was signed by the CBCN President, Archbishop Matthew Man-Oso Ndagoso of Kaduna, and the Conference Secretary, Bishop Peter Olukayode Odetoyinbo of Abeokuta Diocese.

The bishops expressed concern over the continued prevalence of violence, kidnapping, banditry, illegal mining and theft of the nation’s natural resources, saying the situation was threatening peace and national unity.

They also decried attacks on schools and places of worship, as well as the abduction and killing of students and worshippers.

According to them, the displacement of communities has also left millions of Nigerians in Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camps across the country.

The bishops urged the Federal Government to intensify efforts to secure the country and create conditions that would enable displaced persons to return to their ancestral homes.

They called for stronger security forces, improved intelligence gathering and the prosecution of those responsible for criminal activities.

The bishops also urged Nigerians to report suspicious activities, cooperate with security agencies and reject ethnic and religious divisions.

They renewed their call for the decentralisation of the police system, saying policing should serve the common good rather than personal, ethnic, political or religious interests.

On the economy, the CBCN called for the creation of more jobs, an enabling environment for businesses and policies capable of reducing the financial burden on poor Nigerians.

They also urged government to invest transparently in public infrastructure, including roads, electricity, water supply and railway transportation.

2027 Elections

On the 2027 general elections, the bishops called on all stakeholders to work towards free, fair and credible polls.

They encouraged eligible voters to participate in the elections and vote for candidates they considered qualified and in line with their consciences.

The bishops directed dioceses and parishes across the country to undertake civic education and mobilisation, as well as end-of-month fasting and prayer with Rosary processions from October to December 2026.

They declared December 8, 2026, as a special national day of prayer and fasting for the success of the elections.

The bishops also urged citizens to study the pastoral letter issued by the Conference on the forthcoming elections and adhere to its provisions and guidelines.

Bishops Reject Foreign Aid Bill

The CBCN also opposed the Foreign Aids (Regulation, Transparency and Disclosure) Bill, 2026, which it said had passed first and second readings in the National Assembly.

The bishops argued that provisions requiring the registration of foreign aid resources and government supervision of their use could adversely affect churches, mosques, schools and humanitarian organisations providing assistance to vulnerable and conflict-affected communities.

They particularly faulted a provision that allows authorities to deny registration or refuse renewal where an organisation’s activities are deemed “not in the national interest”.

According to the bishops, the provision gives government officials broad discretionary powers and could create an additional layer of bureaucracy and excessive government control over independent civic organisations.

They said non-profit organisations and incorporated trustees, including religious and humanitarian bodies, were already regulated by the Corporate Affairs Commission under the Companies and Allied Matters Act and other applicable laws.

The bishops therefore urged the National Assembly and the Federal Government to discontinue the process of passing the bill into law, citing the need to protect freedom of association, religion, thought and conscience.

Technology, AI

On technology and artificial intelligence, the bishops said technology was not inherently evil but was also not neutral in its application.

They urged Nigerians to deploy technology responsibly and use it to support evangelisation, knowledge creation and development.

The bishops specifically called on politicians and other users of technology to observe ethical standards in the deployment of artificial intelligence, particularly in the period leading to the 2027 elections.

They congratulated the Vice President of the Conference, Archbishop Alfred Adewale Martins of the Lagos Archdiocese, on his appointment to the Dicastery for Evangelisation, Section for First Evangelisation and New Particular Churches.

The bishops also reiterated their call for what they described as renewed politics anchored on moral principles, respect for human life and dignity, and the pursuit of the common good, adding that “all hope is not lost.”

World.title: US appeals court puts brakes on third-country deportations
World.content:
US President Donald Trump speaks after signing executive orders in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, on August 7, 2026. (Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP)

A US federal appeals court on Friday broadly upheld a lower court ruling restricting a Trump administration policy of deporting undocumented migrants to countries that are not their own.

The three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the First Circuit said people facing “third-country” deportations must be given effective notice ahead of time about where they are being sent to allow them to raise concerns about potential persecution.

Congress has made it US policy not to deport people to countries where their lives would be in danger or they could be subject to torture.

“An individual’s right to contest removal to a country based on a fear of persecution in that country means little if one does not receive prior notice of the intended removal destination and a meaningful opportunity to contest that destination,” said Judge Seth Aframe, writing for the unanimous three-judge panel.

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) policy “would deny access to that protection to a substantial swath of noncitizens who are sent to third countries with no notice of their destination,” the judge said.

The Trump administration is expected to appeal the case to the conservative-dominated Supreme Court.

Donald Trump campaigned for president promising to expel millions of undocumented migrants from the United States and has taken a number of actions aimed at speeding up deportations since returning to the White House.

The Trump administration has defended third-country deportations as necessary since the home nations of some of those who are targeted for removal sometimes refuse to accept them.

World.title: Fuel price: Take my idea, rename it, take the credit — Atiku tells Tinubu
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to adopt his proposal for government intervention to bring down petrol prices, telling him to take the idea, rename it and even claim the credit if that would make life easier for Nigerians.

Atiku said Nigerians had borne the consequences of petrol subsidy removal for more than three years, with the shock travelling from filling stations to transport fares, markets, businesses and ultimately household budgets.

He urged Tinubu to use the remaining eight months of his administration to reduce the cost-of-living burden rather than rely on palliatives to cushion policies that, according to him, were making life increasingly unaffordable.

In an address on fuel prices, palliatives and the cost of living, Atiku said the concerns being raised by workers, petroleum marketers, manufacturers and ordinary Nigerians showed that the impact of high energy costs could no longer be dismissed.

“When government makes energy expensive, it makes life expensive. This is no longer an argument between economists. It is the daily reality of millions of Nigerians,” he said.

Atiku recalled that Tinubu had previously dismissed his call for government intervention to reduce petrol prices as showing “serious ignorance” of governance and the economy.

But he said the subsequent experience of Nigerians had demonstrated the need for government to reconsider its approach, asking whether organised labour, petroleum marketers, manufacturers and citizens could all be regarded as ignorant for demanding relief.

“When workers, producers, marketers and ordinary families are all raising the alarm, government must listen,” Atiku said.

He said leadership required the humility to acknowledge when a policy was producing damaging consequences and the courage to change direction.

“Leadership requires the humility to confront the consequences of policy and the courage to change course,” he said.

The former Vice President also questioned the emphasis on GDP growth, increased government revenue and larger allocations, arguing that Nigerians were more concerned about what their incomes could actually buy.

“Government celebrates GDP growth, higher revenues and bigger allocations. But Nigerians judge the economy by what their money can buy,” he said.

According to him, manufacturers were struggling with rising production costs while consumers were losing the purchasing power needed to buy the goods being produced.

“The goods are there. The need is there. What is missing is the purchasing power,” he said.

Atiku therefore called on Tinubu to act on his earlier proposal, insisting that the political ownership of an idea should not matter if its implementation could reduce hardship.

“Bola Tinubu should not be ashamed to do what is necessary to lower the price of petrol simply because Atiku Abubakar proposed a government intervention,” he said.

“He should just take the idea. Rename it if he wishes, and even take the credit. What matters to me is that Nigerians pay less.”

Atiku also rejected reliance on palliatives as the principal response to the cost-of-living crisis, saying temporary relief could not replace policies capable of lowering the underlying cost of production and living.

“Do not make life unbearable and then distribute bags of rice as evidence of compassion. Palliatives manage pain. Good policy addresses the source of the pain,” he said.

Turning to electricity, Atiku warned against a repeat of the petrol subsidy experience as electricity subsidies are expected to be phased out from 2027.

He said households and businesses were already struggling with electricity costs, while manufacturers were spending heavily on electricity, diesel and alternative sources of power to keep their operations running.

“The lesson of petrol must not be repeated with electricity. Do not remove first and think later. Do not impose the pain first and search for palliatives afterwards,” Atiku said.

He urged Tinubu to use the remaining eight months of his tenure to reduce the burden on Nigerians, offering to make his policy framework available to the administration if required.

“Nigerians do not have to wait for another administration before they benefit from an idea that can help them today,” he said.

“If you need the framework, I will provide it. Implement it under your government. Give it whatever name you choose. Take the credit.”

Atiku also outlined his proposed approach to petrol pricing if elected President in 2027, promising a transparent production subsidy for petroleum products refined in Nigeria and sold to Nigerians.

He said the scheme would support domestic refining while ensuring that government intervention translated into lower prices, adding that imported petroleum products would not qualify.

According to him, the programme would have a fixed spending limit, require National Assembly approval and be subject to independent audits.

Atiku likened the proposal to government support for a Nigerian rice miller, saying lower milling costs could translate into cheaper rice, increased demand for locally produced paddy, more business for farmers and additional jobs in processing, packaging and transportation.

He said the same principle should apply to petroleum: government support should be tied to domestic production and lower prices for consumers.

Atiku maintained that the ultimate test of economic reform was its effect on households rather than the size of government revenues or official growth figures.

“I am prepared to compete with you politically. But I will never compete with the welfare of the Nigerian people,” he said.

“The presidency may be contested. The wellbeing of Nigerians should never be.”

He said his proposed economic programme would seek to expand production, create jobs and ensure that economic growth translated into greater purchasing power.

“Ultimately, Nigerians do not live on statistics. They live on what their hard-earned money can buy,” Atiku said.

World.title: Anambra Court jails native doctor ‘Eke Hit’ 12 years
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

AWKA — An Anambra State High Court sitting in Awka has sentenced a native doctor, Ekene Igboekweze, popularly known as “Eke Hit,” to 12 years’ imprisonment for offences arising from alleged kidnapping, protective charms and money rituals.

Justice Jude Obiora sentenced Igboekweze to six years’ imprisonment on each of two counts, with the sentences to run concurrently, without an option of fine. The court also ordered that the period he had already spent in detention be counted as part of the sentence.

Igboekweze and two other suspects were arraigned on April 4, 2025, on charges bordering on conspiracy, kidnapping, protective charms and money rituals.

In his defence, Igboekweze told the court that he was a registered herbalist and a member of the Odinani Okija Traditional Association, adding that his practice involved the use of herbs and roots.

He said the viral videos that made him popular were old and had been recorded before the enactment of the Anambra State Homeland Security Law, 2025.

Delivering judgment, Justice Obiora held that the prosecution had proved counts one and two beyond reasonable doubt, while he resolved count three in favour of the defendant.

Before the sentence was pronounced, Igboekweze pleaded for forgiveness, saying he had learnt his lessons and urging the court to consider his family.

He particularly appealed for consideration of his newborn triplets, whom he said he had not seen since their birth.

His wife, Elizabeth, and half-brother also pleaded for leniency, describing him as well-behaved and kind.

They told the court that Igboekweze was his mother’s only son in a polygamous family and had maintained good character.

Igboekweze, who hails from Umuofor Village, Okija, in Ihiala Local Government Area of Anambra State, was arrested in February 2025 by operatives of the state-sponsored Agunechemba security outfit alongside two other native doctors.

The arrests followed the signing of the Anambra State Homeland Security Law, 2025, by Governor Chukwuma Soludo.

The law prohibits native doctors from claiming that they can make people wealthy through “Oke Ite” and other rituals. It also prohibits the preparation of charms for criminals by native doctors.

Another native doctor, Chidozie Nwangwu, who was earlier sentenced to 11 months’ imprisonment, was on Friday granted pardon by Governor Soludo and appointed youth ambassador for the state.

World.title: 31 confirmed dead after attack at police HQ in Pakistan
World.content:
Army personnel stand amid the rubble following an explosion inside the police headquarters at Kohat in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on September 18, 2026. An explosion at a historic police headquarters in northern Pakistan on September 18 killed at least eight people and wounded 35 more, officials said, with the country’s president swiftly blaming a militant group. (Photo by Basit SHAH / AFP)

The death toll from an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters in northern Pakistan rose to at least 31, including 16 police personnel, a senior police official told AFP on Saturday, with fighting ongoing.

Attackers stormed the Old Police Lines complex at Kohat, a town of around 220,000 people in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, on Friday afternoon.

The police compound serves as a district-level police headquarters, housing key offices of the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), Special Branch and several other police units.

“At least 31 people, including 16 police personnel, have been killed and more than 100 injured so far in the militant attack and suicide bombing,” the official said.

“Several militants are still holed up in the Special Branch section of the Kohat Police Complex,” the police official told AFP on condition of anonymity.

“An exchange of fire with them has been ongoing since late last night. Their exact number remains unclear,” the official added.

A statement from the Kohat district health officer late on Friday said that more than 100 people had been injured, the vast majority of them police personnel, and several were in a critical condition.

Local militant group Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, a faction linked to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) — the Pakistani Taliban — has claimed responsibility for the attack.

– Rubble, blown-out walls –

AFP images showed military personnel standing by piles of bricks, rubble and blown-out walls following the attack, with soldiers carrying assault rifles guarding the complex.

Several ambulances were seen lining a street near the police compound.

Pakistan has blamed the increase in attacks in KP and the southern border province of Balochistan on militancy emanating from Afghanistan, where the Taliban government denies Afghan involvement.

The accusations have sparked a bitter rift and armed conflict between the neighbouring countries, and Pakistan has carried out deadly airstrikes it says target militants on Afghan soil.

The Taliban government in Kabul and the United Nations said dozens of civilians were killed in the latest Pakistani strikes on eastern Afghanistan in June.

Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack on Friday evening, expressing “deep sorrow and regret over the injury of several people as a result of the blast”.

He directed the “best medical assistance be provided to the injured” and called for a report into the attack.

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed “regret” over the casualties, sending his “best wishes for the speedy recovery of those injured in the blast”.

“The complete elimination of Fitna-al-Khawarij and terrorists operating with foreign backing is essential for national security,” he said, using another term for the TTP group.

AFP

World.title: Deaths in custody: FG suspends 20 NSCDC officers, sets up probe panel
World.content:
Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo

By Omeiza Ajayi

The Federal Government has suspended 20 officers of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC and constituted a 10-member independent committee to investigate the reported deaths of 37 people held by the Niger State Command of the Corps on suspicion of illegal mining.

Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, who announced the measures on Saturday in a statement, said the committee was set up following a directive by President Bola Tinubu for “a comprehensive, transparent and unhindered investigation” into the incident, which occurred on Thursday, 17 September 2026.

Describing the deaths as deeply disturbing, the Minister said the government owes the families of the deceased and the Nigerian public a transparent account of the events leading to the incident.

Tunji-Ojo directed the suspension of all officers involved in the incident pending the conclusion of the independent committee’s investigation, and warned the Corps’ leadership and officers against any interference with the process.

“Any attempt to destroy or conceal evidence, intimidate witnesses or obstruct the investigation will be treated as a serious offence,” he warned, while directing the NSCDC leadership and all relevant officers to cooperate fully with the committee and to preserve all records and material evidence connected to the incident for investigators.

According to the statement, the independent committee is expected to establish the identities of the deceased and investigate their arrests, detention, and the cause and circumstances of their deaths.

The minister further directed the committee to determine responsibility, complicity, negligence and misconduct, and to recommend appropriate action, compensation where applicable, and measures to prevent a recurrence.

The committee is chaired by Mr Jonathan Kure, a retired Deputy Director General of the Department of State Services DSS, with Prof. Isa Hayatu Ciroma, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria SAN and former Director General of the Nigeria Law School, as Secretary.

Other members are AIG Hosea Hassan Karma (retired); Prof. Olayinka Buhari, a professor of histopathology and former Chief Medical Director of the University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital; a representative of the Minna Emirate Council; a representative of the Niger State Government; Alhaji Liman Sulaiman, National Secretary of the Miners Association of Nigeria; Mr Deji Adeyanju, lawyer and human rights activist; Mrs Zainab Suleiman Okino of Blueprint Newspaper; and Dr George Agbakahi, a public affairs analyst.

The statement said the committee may co-opt relevant experts, access all necessary facilities and documents, visit relevant locations and request memoranda from members of the public, and has two weeks to complete its work and submit its report to the Minister.

Among those suspended, in addition to the Niger State Commandant of the Corps, are the O/C Station Guard, SC Usman Isah Ndamaka; Station Guard, ASCI Hassan Mohammed; Station Guard, CCA Bala Mohammed; Arresting Officer/O/C Investigation, CSC Oluwadare Sunday; Arresting Officer, DCC Obafemi Elvis; and Arresting Officer, CSC Annas Shitto Lamino. Others are HOD INT/INV, DCC Philip Ajayi; O/C Legal, Barr. Stephen Tsado; Day/Night Duty Officer, ASCI Alhassan Mohammed; and a string of officers listed for guard duty, including IC Abdullahi Sale, IC Mohammed Sonfada, CAI Liman Abubakar, CAI Bala Usman, IC Mohammed Jiya, DSC Isah Suleiman, CAI Ahmed Wushishi, IC Sale Adamu, IC Haruna Mohammed, ASCI Aliyu Sallah and CAI Isah Sanusi.

The Minister extended his condolences to the families of the deceased and appealed for calm while the investigation continues.

World.title: UK’s Disintegration As Prognosis For Federations
World.content:
By Mobolaji Sanusi

“Empires always have the hubris to think they are indestructible, when in fact they are always unsustainable.”—Marianne Williamson(1952 till date).

Nothing in life lasts forever. Not even human life is interminable. Through contractual arrangements, humans and nations have devised legal frameworks that outlive generations. However enduring such arrangements may seem, a day comes when they outlive their usefulness, either by operation of law or through force majeure.

The world have seen this happen with colonial rule in colonies around the world. No matter how long colonial rule lasted, the affected colonies eventually secured their liberation at one point or another. Even the most powerful country in contemporary times, the United States of America, was once colonised by Britain.

Historically, it is interesting to note that England founded Jamestown in Virginia, known as the first permanent English settlement in what is today the United States in 1607. This feat was achieved through the London Company and the Plymouth Company, acting under King James I authority. In 1620, Plymouth Colony in Massachusetts was also founded by English migrants who arrived on the Mayflower.

In essence, the United States was not immune from colonisation. Interestingly by 1732, when the Province of Georgia was founded, the original thirteen English colonies were complete. But the struggle for recognition was trenchant, and by 1776, the country gained its independence and became known as the United States of America. To this day, both countries still maintain sound diplomatic relations based on mutual respect. The expiration of colonial ties between these two countries reflects the impermanence of relationships anywhere in the world.

The world, in subsequent decades, also witnessed the breakup of unified blocs and even the coming together of divided nations whose relationships were once considered historically impenetrable. The fragmentation of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) and the coming together of East and West Germany readily come to mind. The USSR, as a unified bloc, endured for sixty-nine years from its creation on December 30, 1922, until December 26, 1991, when it was formally dissolved.

East and West Germany, in the aftermath of World War II, endured forty-five years of Cold War separation driven by the Allied powers and the Soviet-led communist bloc. West Germany came into existence on May 23, 1949, while East Germany was formed in October 1949. The Berlin Wall, built in 1961, separated the two Cold War-induced countries, which share a common ancestry and identity, until the Wall fell in November 1989 and the two countries reunified on October 3, 1990.

Nothing, whether brought together by forceful, peaceful, or natural means, lasts forever. It is with this benefit of hindsight that the coordinated attempts by the leaders of Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland to seek self-determination from Westminster have become instructive. The three entities, perhaps inevitably, now perceive their current political arrangement under Westminster as unsustainable.

John Swinney of Scotland and Michelle O’Neill of Northern Ireland called for an independence-seeking referendum and an Irish reunification poll, respectively. However, Wales’ Rhun ap Iorwerth gave approval for a declaration of self-determination but showed reticence in agreeing to a timeframe for a referendum on Welsh independence. One thing, however, is incontrovertible: the unwavering resolve of the three nations to stand alone as independent countries outside the United Kingdom framework. Their historic meeting of September 14, 2026, in Cardiff, Wales, created a solid platform affirming their commitment to this independence plan. The fact that the leaders of the governments of these nations are from nationalist parties has only catalysed the process of seeking a break away from the United Kingdom.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is insisting that independence referendums cannot occur for now, which is albeit a temporary foreclosure of any imminent breakup. But for how long can Westminster stand in the way of the independence desires of these nations? This is in view of the fact that they have the democratic right to decide their own constitutional future through a referendum on independence or unification.

Westminster needs to realise that whatever has a beginning must have an end, and the demands for independence by these three nations should not be an exception. Retrospectively, Westminster should be a good student of history and not be unduly recalcitrant. For example, Wales was historically annexed and became part of the Kingdom of England under the Laws in Wales Acts of 1535 and 1542.

Scotland, in the same vein, joined the political union through the Acts of Union 1707. The passage of the Acts ended the period of shared monarchy that had existed since 1603 and created a single Kingdom of Great Britain. The Kingdom of Ireland was merged with the Kingdom of Great Britain through the Acts of Union 1800 to form the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland in 1801. By 1922, when most of Ireland seceded to become the Irish Free State (now the Republic of Ireland), six counties in Ulster remained with the United Kingdom as Northern Ireland.

As it happened in the United States, the old USSR, and even Germany, the United Kingdom, under Westminster’s political control in London, must be willing and ready to accede to the requests of these three nations to leave the United Kingdom union.

What is happening in the United Kingdom should serve as a clear admonition to federations across the globe that no arrangement can outlive its expiry date.

All federations anywhere in the world should be responsive to contemporary realities. The United Kingdom and other countries in similar situations have no option but to accede to the demands of the component units of their political system once clear desires for independence are expressed.

Lest we forget that Edward Gibbon once observed in The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire that “All that is human must retrograde.” Who knows whether, like other human-contrived kingdoms that have hitherto existed, the grave of the monolithic United Kingdom might inevitably be awaiting its corpse, even though this might take a little while to happen? This gate also applies to other epileptic federations across the world. I rest my case for this week.

Prof. Shaffdeen Amuwo at 80

“Aging is not lost youth but a new stage of opportunity and strength.” —Betty Friedan (1921-2006)

Professor Shaffdeen Amuwo, CON, an elder statesman of repute and one of Nigeria’s remarkable exports to the outside world, specifically the United States of America, celebrated his eightieth birthday on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, with a family prayer at his Ikoyi residence.

In Chicago and the entire United States, this respectable man of character has become renowned, first for his exploits in his chosen field of medicine, where he attained its apogee by becoming a professor, and second for his steadfast commitment to the cause of humanity and his unimpeachable character/integrity.

His life so far is replete with examples worth emulating by true patriots. He is highly self-effacing despite his undeniable accomplishments and influence. This revered addition to the octogenarian group of elders in this great country hardly flaunts his importance and influence.

Apart from the late Dr. Nurudeen Olowopopo, it is doubtful whether there is any living Nigerian who commands the childhood respect, trust and confidence of President Bola Tinubu, GCFR, like Professor Amuwo. Yet, he remains easy-going and devoid of any scandal that usually trails such men with vast connections in the corridors of power.

No wonder his close knit 80th birthday prayer was well attended by the high and mighty in Lagos power circles and beyond. Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu led the pack. His deputy and incoming Governor of Lagos State, insha Allah, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, Bode Agoro, the Head of Service of Lagos State, among other notables, attended the ceremony. The president might have possibly attended if not for his currently being on vacation.

Yours sincerely received the invitation directly from the octogenarian, but for reasons beyond my control that took me out of the state, I could not attend, although I was there in spirit. My apologies, sir, for my excusable absence.

Kindly note sir that you remain our pride, a worthy model and a patriot of inestimable value.

Happy birthday and long may you live for several more years in good health sir.

•Sanusi, former MD/CEO of Lagos State Signage and  Agency, is currently Managing Partner at AMS RELIABLE SOLICITORS. (WhatsApp only: 07011117777

World.title: 2027: Where Are the Women?
World.content:
*Only 9.6% of candidates are women*Groups call for deliberate commitment to gender balance

Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and Sunday Ehigiator in Lagos

Ahead of the 2027 general election, the final lists of all the candidates cleared by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) have shown that women remain significantly underrepresented among the candidates vying for various elective positions, constituting only 9.65 per cent, far below the 35 per cent affirmative action.

The data from the final lists of candidates recently published by the electoral body indicated that a total of 4,881 candidates were cleared for the three elections.



However, of this number, 471 are women, representing 9.65 per cent, while 4,410 are men, representing 90.35 per cent.

A further breakdown of the lists by category showed a huge gap among the National Assembly candidates.

For the presidential election, out of 18 candidates, only two are women, representing 11.11 per cent, whereas 16 are men, representing 88.89 per cent.



The two female presidential candidates are Okwori Fredrick of the National Democratic Party (NDP) and Okereke Esther of the National Rescue Movement (NRM).

Similarly, for the senatorial election, 1,303 candidates were cleared by INEC, out of which 123 are women, representing 9.44 per cent, while 1,180 are men, representing 90.56 per cent.



Also, for the House of Representatives, a total of 3,560 candidates were cleared by the commission, out of which 346 are women, constituting 9.72 per cent, whereas 3,214 are men, constituting 90.28 per cent.

Analysis of the 123 female senatorial candidates shows that Akwa Ibom has the highest number, with 10 candidates, followed by Rivers, Osun and Kwara states, with seven candidates each.



The seven female candidates for Kwara State are Temako Naomi, Ibrahim Ramat, Owolabi Felicia, Adesola Kehinde, Abdulahi Motunrayo, Abdulkarim-Adisa Maryam Ayoola-Fadekemi and Anifowoshe Grace.

The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) has four female senatorial candidates, including Omotosho Ololade, Ireti Kingibe, Austenpeters-Pam Amanda and Benyeogor Ufedojo.



However, several states have only one female senatorial candidate, including Adamawa (Bagardi Charity); Borno (Baba Gana Zannah); Ebonyi (Nwachi Ude); Ondo (Omolabaro Omotilewa); Sokoto (Abdulrahman Halima); and Kebbi (Kabir Mohammed). Bauchi State has two candidates.



In the same vein, for the House of Representatives, Lagos leads with 31 female candidates, followed by Imo with 21, Anambra with 20, Rivers with 20, Akwa Ibom with 17, Delta with 17 and Oyo with 17.

Kwara State also has 16 female candidates for the Green Chamber, while states like Katsina, Nasarawa and Zamfara have only one female candidate each.



Responding, the Communication Manager, Nigerian Women Trust Fund, Mujidat Agbabiaka, said the data was not simply a question about the number of women appearing on the ballot.



“It raises a broader question about whether the political system is providing women with a genuinely accessible pathway into political leadership. These statistics point to the fact that 471 out of 4,881 candidates are women; that is approximately 9.6 per cent.

“In other words, fewer than one in ten candidates is a woman. That is not simply a question about the number of women appearing on the ballot; it raises a broader question about whether the political system is providing women with a genuinely accessible pathway into political leadership.



“This is another call that every political party must make a deliberate commitment to more gender balance and inclusion.”

In her contribution, the Project Officer, Renevlyn Development Initiative, Tracy Ohovwore, said: “The minimal inclusion and abysmal representation of women in all strata of government and in political activities in Nigeria is the reflection of a deep and worrying trend in our society. Even when women get slots, such positions are presented as merely ticking off the box, and not necessarily a rightfully deserved position. The implication is that pressing issues concerning women take the back seat and are treated with levity.”



Executive Director, Rule of Law and Accountability Advocacy Centre (RULAAC), Okechukwu Nwanguma, pointed out that the 9.6 per cent “raises serious concerns about the continuing underrepresentation of women in Nigeria’s political process.”

“For a country in which women constitute roughly half of the population, their persistently low presence among candidates for major elective offices points to structural barriers that continue to restrict equal political participation.



“These include the high cost of electoral politics, unequal access to political networks and campaign financing, discriminatory social attitudes, political violence and intimidation, and internal party processes that may disadvantage women seeking nominations,” he added.



According to him, “Nigeria also needs to revisit broader legal and policy measures aimed at improving women’s political representation, including the continuing debate around special or reserved seats and other affirmative-action mechanisms. Any such measures should be transparently designed and consistent with constitutional and democratic principles.



“The 9.6 per cent figure should therefore prompt serious reflection about the inclusiveness of Nigeria’s democracy. Elections should provide meaningful opportunities for every segment of society to participate, compete and be represented.”

World.title: Tension, Outrage Trail Death Of 37 Miners in NSCDC Detention
World.content:
*Tinubu orders probe, vows punishment for anyone responsible

*Babangida, Obi, CSOs condemn deaths, Bago declares 24-hour curfew

* NSCDC Niger commandant removed, riot breaks out in Minna

*Survivor says chemical sprayed in detention room made breathing difficukt

*Nassarawa bans minors from mining

* Another five alleged illegal miners die in Taraba pit collapse

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha, Michael Olugbode, Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja, Igbawase Ukumba in Lafia, Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt and Laleye Dipo in Minns

Tension and outrage yesterday gripped Niger State following the deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), as President Bola Tinubu ordered a full and transparent investigation into the tragedy and vowed that anyone found responsible would face punishment.

Their death followed enforcement of operations around Lt.Gen. Mohammed Inuwa Wushishi Estate in Minna, Niger State.

This comes as five alleged illegal miners were also confirmed dead yesterday, following the collapse of a mining pit in Mayokam village, located in Bali Local Government Area of Taraba State. The Taraba State Police said five miners were dug out of the collapsed pit following efforts by local residents.

In a related development, Nassarawa state government announced the ban of underage miners as it is now an offence in the state for anyone below the age of 18 to work in any mine.

In Niger, mourning the tragedy, former military President, General Ibrahim Babangida lamented the tragedy and called for calm but advocates measures to ensure that such never repeats.

This was as Governor Umar Bago of Niger State declared a 24-hour curfew ion Minna following breakdown of law and order over riots which broke out over the death of the detainees in custody of Civil Defence in the state.

The suspected illegal miners were among scores of people arrested by the NSCDC during enforcement operations against illegal mining in the M.I. Wushishi/Lukoto area of Niger State on September 15 and 16. The Corps had said the operation was aimed at tackling illegal mining and resulted in the recovery of various exhibits.

Their deaths were reported in the early hours of September 17, shortly after the arrests. The Niger State NSCDC Command had initially said the detainees died following a suspected disease outbreak and that their remains had been deposited at the General Hospital, Minna, for medical examination. The national headquarters subsequently cautioned that no specific disease had been established as the cause of death pending medical and laboratory examinations.

But in what appears as an early clue to what led to the death of the alleged illegal miners, a survivor (names withheld) narrated that officials who took them for detention sprayed chemical in the place which made breathing difficukt before the people choked to death. He however did not name the chemical.

Also, Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, called for a transparent and independent investigation.

While reports have raised issues including disease, overcrowding and inadequate ventilation, the actual cause of the deaths is yet to be conclusively established. Authorities have said investigations, including medical examinations and autopsies, are being conducted to determine the cause.

President Tinubu in a statement by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, directed relevant authorities to ensure that the investigation was comprehensive, transparent and unhindered, covering the circumstances of the arrests, the condition of the detainees when they were taken into custody, the conditions under which they were detained, the number of persons held in the facility, the medical attention provided and the events leading to their deaths.

“The suspension of officers is only an administrative step and must not substitute for a proper determination of criminal responsibility where the evidence warrants prosecution”, he said.

Tinubu directed the Ministry of Interior and the NSCDC leadership to cooperate fully with all relevant investigative authorities and ensure that no officer interferes with the process or attempts to frustrate the establishment of the truth.

The President stressed the importance of the life of every Nigerian and that no citizen should lose his life while in government custody as a result of negligence, abuse, inhumane treatment or dereliction of duty.

Tinubu expressed deep concern over the reported deaths, describing the development as a grave matter that requires urgent investigation and accountability.

According to him: “While the federal government would continue to combat illegal mining and other criminal activities across the country, enforcement operations must be conducted strictly within the law and with full respect for the dignity and fundamental rights of every person in custody.

“The fact that these individuals were suspected of illegal mining does not in any way remove their right to life, dignity and humane treatment while in government custody. Government will not tolerate mass deaths arising from official negligence, dereliction of duty or failure by public officials to protect the lives placed under their care.

“Where the investigation establishes that any official, through action, abuse or negligence, contributed to these deaths, such an officer must be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law. There must be accountability.”

The President extended his condolences to the families of the deceased and prayed for the repose of their souls.

He also appealed for calm among the families and communities affected by the tragedy, assuring them that the Federal Government would pursue the truth and take appropriate action based on credible evidence.

Babangida Condemns Deaths, Mourn

Former military President General Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida condemned the death of the 37 Illegal Miners in NSCDC custody in Minna Niger State.

General Babangida described the incident as not only “tragic” but “deeply disturbing,”

The former military president in a statement made available to newsmen in Minna yesterday signed on his behalf by the Tambari Kagara Alhaji Danladi Umar Abdulhameed urged all parties concerned in the unfortunate incident “to toe the path of peace in the interest of peaceful coexistence”

The former military president commended the steps already taken by the Niger state government to douse tension saying that the postponement of the APC campaign flag off set for Saturday by the government was an indication of its people oriented policy.

According to General Babangida, “the steps being taken by the authorities are necessary to establish the facts surrounding the deaths and ensure that appropriate action is taken based on the findings.”

General Babangida expressed condolences to the parents and families of the deceased, as well as the people and Government of Niger State over the loss of lives in the unfortunate incident.

NSCDC Commandant Suspended

The NSCDC yesterday removed its Niger State Commandant from operational duties and commenced a full-scale investigation into the deaths of illegal miners who were in the custody of the Corps.

The development followed an order by the Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, directing the Commandant General of the NSCDC, Prof Ahmed Audi, to conduct a transparent and unhindered probe into the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

Acting on the minister’s directive, Audi ordered the Niger State Commandant to immediately step aside and report to the NSCDC National Headquarters in Abuja to appear before the panel constituted to investigate the incident.

The state commandant’s Heads of Operations, Mining, Legal, Intelligence, and Investigation were also directed to report to the national headquarters and face the inquiry panel.

To ensure continuity of command and prevent any disruption to operations in the state, the NSCDC Commandant General directed another commandant to proceed to Niger State and assume immediate control of the command.

The Corps, in statement signed by the NSCDC National Public Relations Officer, Assistant Commandant of Corps Babawale Afolabi, said the investigation would establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths and determine whether any personnel breached the law, operational procedures or professional standards in handling the detainees.

Audi assured the Interior Minister that the investigation would be comprehensive and that any officer found culpable would face appropriate administrative or disciplinary action and, where necessary, criminal proceedings under extant laws.

The NSCDC said the probe was also intended to reinforce accountability within its ranks, particularly in the discharge of its statutory responsibilities relating to illegal mining and the protection of critical national assets.

The Corps stressed that the enforcement of its mandate must be conducted within the framework of the law, while safeguarding the dignity, safety and fundamental rights of persons in its custody.

Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago, also announced that the “Commandant of the NSCDC in Minna and his team have been suspended to pave way for thorough investigation into the matter.”

Bago disclosed that a panel has started meeting adding that the “Director General of the NSCDC, who is currently out of the country, has delegated his deputy to represent him,” adding that the state government had already met with the senior NSCDC official.

There was palpable tension in Minna yesterday following the action of youths who set fire on tyres on the highways and obstructed vehicular movements.
