World.title: Parties step up work on candidate lists ahead of March Riigikogu elections
World.content:
With less than half a year until the Riigikogu elections, Estonia's major political parties are assembling candidate lists and drafting election programs. Some have already begun campaigning, while others will finalize their lists and platforms only in January.

EKRE Ready even for snap elections

EKRE parliamentary group adviser Aarne Mäe said preparations for candidate lists have been underway for some time. "Because of the possibility of snap elections, we have accelerated the process," Mäe said.

"If we proceed at the usual pace, we will hold our internal elections in November, as required by the party statutes. That's when the order of candidates in each district will be determined. The general list will be approved by the party council at the beginning of January," he added.

Social Democrats campaigning for lower food VAT

Social Democratic Party secretary‑general Piret Hartman said their list‑building is also ongoing. "In fact, it started already in spring. Districts will make final decisions on candidates and their order at the end of the year. The general list will be approved at the general assembly on January 16," she said.

Hartman noted that campaigning is already underway. "We are actively meeting people across regions, attending events and organizing activities. At the moment we also have an outdoor campaign in several districts focused on lowering VAT on food. We will roll out larger campaign events in October–November. The election program will be approved at the January general assembly," Hartman said.

Eesti 200 preparing as part of everyday politics

Eesti 200 executive director Anneli Kannus said the party does not treat election preparations as a separate process.

"For the party, politics is everyday work. It's difficult to view election preparation as something separate from ongoing discussions or work in the Riigikogu and government. Plans are made continuously as part of normal activity. Eesti 200's more detailed election plans will be finalized in the coming months," Kannus said.

Center Party gathering proposals from regions

Center Party secretary‑general Anneli Ott said the party is drafting its platform and collecting proposals from regional branches. "We also have ongoing meetings with representatives of various interest groups, both in the parliamentary faction and at the party office," Ott said.

She added that regional branches are currently working on candidate lists in their districts, and the party is waiting for their proposals.

The election slogan will be decided once the main focus of the platform becomes clear. "Today the timeline for lists, the platform and the slogan is still open," Ott said.

Isamaa: Some people don't yet know they'll be candidates

Isamaa secretary‑general Andres Metsoja said preparations have been underway for at least half a year.

"Since spring, various program working groups have been meeting, open to all party members. The last meetings were held this week, and discussions with professional organizations will continue in the coming months. At Tuesday's leadership meeting, we agreed to compile all ideas by the end of September for a full overview. We will also cost our core promises, because the last years under Reform Party leadership have pushed public finances into such deep crisis that promising rivers of milk and mountains of porridge is impossible. We must show how we will fund our commitments," Metsoja said.

Work on candidate lists is happening in parallel. "Many well‑known politicians, community leaders and experts from various fields — including those not previously involved in politics — have agreed to run. It's too early to name names, and certainly there are people in Estonia who don't yet know they will be candidates on Isamaa's list. That's why program work is so important — to communicate Isamaa's vision for Estonia's future and give people the chance to contribute," Metsoja said.

He pointed to the summer mini‑campaign "Eesti asi on parim asi" ("Estonian things are the best things"). "Our regional branches are now carrying that message forward by visiting food producers, industrial companies and other contributors to Estonia's economy," he said.

The main Riigikogu campaign will begin after New Year. "But of course we are ready to present our vision earlier if snap elections are called," Metsoja added.

Reform Party to announce lead candidates in November

Reform Party secretary‑general Kristo Enn Vaga confirmed that work on candidate lists and the election program is underway, with both set to be approved at the January general assembly.

"We will announce our lead candidates during November. The campaign kickoff will be on October 17 at the party council meeting in Tartu," Vaga said.

Parempoolsed began pre‑campaign in summer

Parempoolsed currently have just one party switcher MP, a former Eesti 200 member Kalev Stoicescu, but the party is polling above the electoral threshold. Parempoolsed are also assembling their lists, and their pre‑campaign began in late summer.

"We believe Parempoolsed will have strong lists, and right‑leaning voters will find suitable candidates to support," said party vice-chair Kristjan Vanaselja.

"Unlike parliamentary parties, our campaign resources are limited and taxpayer funding is minimal. We use the opportunity to be visible when advertising is cheaper than during the active campaign period. Parempoolsed will run another short campaign in autumn. The slogan and unified campaign will be unveiled in December–January, when the full program and lists are finalized," Vanaselja said.

The next Riigikogu election will take place on March 7 next year.

World.title: Justice chancellor challenges Estonia's new retirement age system
World.content:
Justice Chancellor Ülle Madise is questioning a new retirement age system that could mean people in Estonia born in the same year start receiving a pension at different times.

Under the new system, which takes effect in 2027, Estonia's official retirement age will be set separately for each calendar year based on changes in life expectancy, affecting when people become eligible for an old-age pension.

As chancellor of justice, Madise questioned whether a calendar year-based system assigning different retirement ages based on birth month is constitutional. She cited Tallinn University (TLÜ) professor and demographer Lauri Leppik, who outlined the issue in the university's demography blog last year.

"People born in January have a retirement age one to three months lower than those born in December of the same year, unless the calculated retirement age for that particular calendar year happens to be a whole number of years," Leppik wrote, also explaining that the dividing line for different treatment would shift from year to year as well.

The difference could have a direct financial impact. Based on the average old-age pension at the time, Leppik noted that a one-month difference in retirement age would mean roughly one additional monthly pension payment, or €825. A two- or three-month difference, however, would mean a difference of €1,650 or €2,475, respectively.

Madise found that the Riigikogu's decision to link Estonia's retirement age to changes in the life expectancy of 65-year-olds is consistent with section 28, paragraph 2 of the Constitution.

The question, she said, is whether setting the age by calendar year is constitutional when it means people born in the same year can end up eligible for a pension at different ages.

Same year, different wait

For example, some people born in the same year could reach retirement age at 65 years and three months, while others would have to wait until 65 and six months.

"Someone may be very disappointed to learn that their retirement age has been pushed back by as much as three months compared with a coworker born in the same year," Madise said.

She questioned whether the state has convincing evidence to justify the difference — for example, evidence that people born in December 1962 have a two-month longer average life expectancy than those born between January and November of the same year.

The justice chancellor has asked the Riigikogu's Social Affairs Committee to promptly discuss the issue and explain why, starting next year, people born in the same year could face different retirement ages based on their month of birth.

World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Four decisive fixtures will wrap up Matchday 8 of the Iraq Stars League on Saturday evening, September 19, 2026, setting the stage for high-stakes clashes spanning the title chase, mid-table consolidation, and redemption campaigns.

Ghaz Al-Shamal takes on Newroz in an encounter where both clubs will battle to secure maximum points and strengthen their footholds in the league standings. World.title: US dollar surges past 160,000 IQD amid US liquidity pressures and market slump
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar crossed the 160,000-dinar threshold across Iraq’s parallel currency markets during opening trading on Saturday, September 19, 2026, marking a sharp depreciation of the domestic currency as market liquidity contracted under geopolitical and fiscal strains.

Bureaus in Baghdad posted selling prices of 160,000 dinars per $100 against buying rates of 159,500 dinars, while trading in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, reflected a parallel surge, settling at 159,650 dinars for sale and 159,100 dinars for purchase.

The widening spread against the Central Bank of Iraq’s official peg of 131,000 dinars follows reports of heightened U.S. Treasury pressure and restrictions on monthly physical cash shipments from Iraq’s oil revenue reserves held at the U.S. Federal Reserve.

Washington has reportedly conditioned the continuity of unhindered dollar liquidity flows on Baghdad’s progress in disarming Iran-aligned armed factions and meeting the critical September 30 deadline, which coincides with the scheduled conclusion of the International Coalition’s military presence.

The resulting cash shortage has fueled market speculation, with local traders and currency dealers warning that selling rates could climb toward the 170,000-dinar mark if physical inflows remain constrained.

The monetary volatility has begun depressing consumer sentiment across the country ahead of the month-end deadline. Households across Iraqi governorates have visibly shifted toward precautionary saving and defensive spending, prioritizing essential food commodities while curtailing expenditures on discretionary goods and leisure services.

Foot traffic and commercial turnover have contracted noticeably across cafes, restaurants, and retail markets—even extending to school stationery vendors preparing for the upcoming academic term—choking domestic cash flow and deepening liquidity bottlenecks across the real economy.

World.title: Iraq Customs clarifies duties on pharmaceuticals, vitamins, and supplements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi General Authority of Customs asserted on Friday evening, September 18, 2026, that the formal classification of imported commodities and the determination of their corresponding Harmonized System (HS) codes and tariff bands remain the exclusive legal jurisdiction of the customs authority.

In a statement received IraqiNews.com, the authority clarified the operative tariff schedules for healthcare products, noting that certified pharmaceutical products are levied at a baseline duty of 0.5%, while vitamins and dietary supplements face duties of either 5% or 10% based on technical categorization.

Customs regulators emphasized that receiving testing clearances or regulatory approvals from the Ministry of Health does not automatically classify a product as a pharmaceutical medicine for border assessment purposes.

The authority underlined that health sector certifications fulfill domestic safety compliance requirements, whereas border taxation, HS code designation, and duty assessments are determined strictly through official statutory tariff tables and active customs regulations.

Under the declared tariff structure, conventional pharmaceuticals formally categorized under recognized medical subheadings qualify for the lower 0.5% rate.

Conversely, vitamins and nutritional supplements are evaluated individually based on their specific chemical formulation, physical composition, and technical commodity descriptions, subjecting them to standard 5% or 10% duty brackets rather than pharmaceutical exemptions.

The authority reiterated that brand names, marketing designations, or laboratory review bodies do not dictate tariff bands, which rely solely on technical HS documentation.

The regulatory clarification addresses recurring friction between border revenue authorities and the domestic healthcare market regarding import costs. In January 2026, the General Authority of Customs confirmed a 1% tariff adjustment on medical supplies, dismissing claims of a ten-fold duty increase flagged by the Iraqi Syndicate of Pharmacists as an unintentional clerical error.

The latest customs advisory establishes clear statutory boundaries between health testing protocols and fiscal border valuations, maintaining firm oversight over revenue collection on non-essential health and wellness supplements entering the country.

World.title: Iraqi Election Commission monitors Russian elections in Moscow
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A senior delegation from Iraq’s Independent High Electoral Commission (IHEC), headed by the Chairman of the Board of Commissioners, Judge Omar Ahmed Mohammed, commenced official international election monitoring duties in the Russian Federation on Friday, September 18, 2026.

The delegation, which includes Chief Electoral Officer Hussein Abdul-Sada Baheer and Board of Commissioners member Abbas Farhan, is participating as accredited international observers for the Russian State Duma parliamentary elections running through September 20, following a formal invitation extended by the Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation.

IHEC confirmed in an official statement that the visit is designed to enhance institutional cooperation, facilitate knowledge exchange on electoral administration, and examine international frameworks for staging large-scale voting processes.

Alongside their direct oversight roles, the Iraqi delegation is taking part in the international forum entitled “Elections in Times of Turmoil,” an expert convening addressing technical, logistical, and administrative mechanisms required to organize and secure democratic balloting under exceptional operational constraints and shifting geopolitical realities.

As part of their official itinerary, the Iraqi commissioners initiated field inspection rounds across several designated polling stations to observe on-the-ground voting workflows firsthand.

The monitoring tour focused on evaluating voting machine operations, logistical organization, ballot management, and queue protocols inside voting centers. IHEC noted that participating in high-level overseas monitoring missions forms a core element of its strategy to benchmark international best practices, integrate comparative operational knowledge, and refine Iraq’s domestic technical and administrative capacities for future electoral cycles.

World.title: Iraq and France work on energy pipeline to Europe
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — France is working with Iraq and Jordan on a pipeline project to transport Iraqi oil and gas to European markets, French President Emmanuel Macron said days after Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi visited Paris for discussions on energy and investment.

Macron stated that the initiative was part of attempts to secure an alternate energy supply for Europe, since the Middle East crisis interrupts conventional shipping routes and raises oil and gas costs.

Iraqi official media said that the planned pipeline would take Iraqi energy via Jordan to European markets.

The statement comes after Al-Zaidi’s official visit to France from September 13 to 14, during which he met with Macron at the Élysée Palace.

The two leaders addressed diversifying energy supply pathways in the wake of delays to Iraqi oil shipments and increased pressure on global energy markets.

During the visit, Iraq and TotalEnergies, a French energy giant, agreed to initiate negotiations on further energy projects, including gas supply collaboration.

TotalEnergies is also looking for a share in the multinational consortium implementing the proposed Basra-Baniyas pipeline, which would give Iraqi petroleum an alternative route from southern oilfields to Syria’s Mediterranean coast, circumventing the Strait of Hormuz.

Chevron, TI Capital, and UCC Holdings of Qatar are all members of the partnership.

The projects highlight Iraq’s quickening efforts to diversify export routes after interruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, which revealed the risk of depending mainly on southern marine terminals for petroleum shipments.

Macron said that Middle Eastern turmoil has exacerbated Europe’s energy challenges, making alternative oil and gas suppliers even more crucial.

France is also advocating for more international cooperation on energy stockpiles and supply, while prices stay high.

For Iraq, new pipeline links via Jordan and Syria might give alternate routes to European clients while lessening its vulnerability to outages in the Arabian Gulf.

World.title: England can build on World Cup ‘spirit’, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said England will build on the “fantastic spirit” of their World Cup campaign as he targets glory on home soil at Euro 2028.

The England boss was speaking at Wembley after naming a 27-man group for a four-game Nations League camp, starting with a clash against world champions Spain on September 26.

It comes just nine weeks after the end of the World Cup, where England conceded two late goals in a painful semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Cole Palmer were the headline picks after both were controversially overlooked for the World Cup.

Tuchel also included Liverpool’s teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite in his first squad since the tournament in North America.

A number of players who were in the World Cup squad including John Stones, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson and Dean Henderson missed out through injury.

Former Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Tuchel said he did not see the Nations League as a new start, instead focusing on continuity.

“I feel that it’s not a new beginning that we are starting now, so we build on a solid and very valuable foundation, and the target is to win the home Euros,” he told reporters on Friday.

Euro 2028 will be co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.

The German said his side’s ultimate failure at the World Cup had left him unfulfilled but stuck by his squad picks.

“I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic,” he said.

“I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.”

Tuchel said Palmer had impressed for Chelsea early in the season.

“He has his numbers back, he has assists back, he has decisive goals back, so that’s why he’s in the squad and I think he has a point to prove,” he said.

“The same goes for Trent. He was never off the list, he was never in a non-selectable class, and he has this chance to show, to be the best version of himself.”

Tuchel said it was his “duty” to play Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo after he failed to feature for a single minute at the World Cup.

The England boss welcomed the challenge of taking on Spain at Wembley.

“We feel the gap is closing and we feel that we are close and we want a proof of point,” he said.

“The stadium is sold out, it will be very exciting, the motivation cannot be higher to play against the world champions.”

England also play the Czech Republic twice and Croatia once during the upcoming international window.

World.title: Anti-Assad music star makes triumphant return to Syria
World.content:
Damascus – Syrian singer Assala Nasri has made a triumphant return to Damascus with a sold-out concert following 15 years of exile due to her opposition to ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad.

Thousands of fans welcomed the 57-year-old, known mononymously as Assala, at a venue in the Syrian capital where she bowed and opened the show with songs hailing the Syrian people.

“Souls of my heart, I missed you,” she repeatedly said to endless cheers on Thursday night.

“My loves, my people, I swear, until this moment I could not believe that I am among you. I want to tell you how much I dreamt of this.”

There was a heavy security presence for the concert, after some religious conservatives launched a campaign calling for its cancellation.

Half of the show’s proceeds will be donated to charity.

Syria’s new Islamist authorities, who overthrew Assad in 2024, have welcomed Assala. Culture Minister Mohammed Yassine Saleh has dubbed her “the daughter of Damascus”.

Joining her on stage, he said her return was that of “every honest Syrian and every free person”.

– ‘Moving forward’ –

Assala was among the first artists to express support for the peaceful anti-Assad protests that erupted in 2011, refusing to partake in events supporting his government.

She was booted from the Syrian artists’ union for her stance and was the target of media campaigns.

She went into exile, living in Cairo with her family and playing shows in various Arab countries.

The bloody repression of the protests led to a 13-year civil war that killed more than half-a-million people.

At Assala’s show, small Syrian flags rippled in time with the music, with many in the crowd unable to hold back their tears.

“I never thought this day would come. It’s like a beautiful dream,” concert-goer Sawsan Wadha, 56, said.

“We are very happy that our country is moving forward,” added 40-year-old Lynn Nahas.

On her new record, “The Syrian Album”, Assala covers folk songs from all 14 of Syria’s provinces as an homage to her country’s cultural diversity.

She sings for the cities scarred by war, but also for the coastline in mourning after last year’s killing of hundreds of members of Assad’s Alawite minority, and for Druze-majority Sweida, which also saw sectarian violence.

– Recovery through art –

Assala’s piercing, powerful voice rang out as she made her way through the album’s tracks at Thursday’s concert.

She also performed fan favourites like “Samehtak” and “Sandooq”, with the jubilant, tearful crowd singing along.

Assala and her family only returned to Damascus this week. An antiques dealer in the capital returned the oud, or Oriental lute, that had belonged to her father, a celebrated musician.

Conservative Muslim figures had expressed criticism in the run-up to the concert.

Egyptian preacher Hani Dahab, who lives in Syria, launched a social media campaign with the slogan “Cancel the Sinful Concerts”. He accused the culture ministry of seeking to “give society a secular character”.

Syrian Salafi preacher Abdul Razzaq al-Mahdi condemned what he called a “concert of music and debauchery”, while a group of preachers in Damascus called on the culture minister to take into account “the religious identity of society”.

While not addressing the critics directly, Assala said at the show that “recovery will only happen with art and music”.

Syria has seen a cultural boom since 2025, but also the rise of preachers and conservative religious movements in public spaces and at universities, raising fears of restrictions on freedom.

Farah Al-Atassi, political advisor to the government, said poetry, language and thought were “an integral part of Syrian identity”.

“This is the Syria that we know and that will endure,” she told AFP.

World.title: UNESCO can be ‘moderator’ in AI debate: chief to AFP
World.content:
Paris – UNESCO chief Khaled el-Enany has proposed in an interview with AFP that the UN culture and education agency become a facilitator in the worldwide wrangling on the risks of artificial intelligence.

“I believe we are uniquely positioned to make UNESCO a true moderator in this global debate,” he said as he prepared to welcome Pope Leo XIV, a key advocate for international AI governance, in Paris next week.

The UN educational, scientific and cultural organisation has long stressed that its remit covers more than heritage, looking to advance in areas ranging from access to education to the ethical use of artificial intelligence.

The debate over the potential dangers of self-improving algorithms has surged in recent weeks, with some researchers warning the technology could end humanity, and leaders of AI companies suggesting development needed to be slowed down.

US President Donald Trump has on the other hand called the fears a “hoax”.

Enany told AFP: “There is a risk that it will get out of control if we don’t intervene.”

“This break, this dialogue that has taken place over the past few weeks, is something very positive,” he added in the interview on Thursday.

He said the cultural agency had found an “indispensable partner” in the pontiff, who is to visit the UNESCO headquarters in Paris on Friday next week at the start of a four-day trip to France.

“This visit will be the beginning of a very solid partnership to strengthen and protect human dignity in this industrial revolution,” Enany said.

It will be the first visit by a pope to UNESCO headquarters since John Paul II in 1980.

– AI ‘must be governed’ –

Pope Leo, the first US pope, this week warned against delegating to algorithms decisions that should be taken by humans alone.

In his first major document, the encyclical “Magnifica Humanitas” (Magnificent Humanity), published in May, the pope issued a call to “disarm” AI in order to “prevent it from dominating humanity”.

Enany said UNESCO had long been concerned with regulating AI, in 2021 issuing a “Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence”.

The guide warned about the risk of violations of privacy and the concentration of technological power in the hands of a few states or companies, and well as potential effects on democracy and the environment.

AI is “an extraordinary tool, but one that must be governed in an ethical, inclusive, and fair way,” Enany said.

Trump has since returning to office withdrawn the United States from UNESCO, alleging that it is biased against Israel and promotes “divisive” causes.

China — one of the major global AI players — has become the agency’s largest donor.

Trump had already ordered a departure from UNESCO in 2017 during his first term, before President Joe Biden reestablished US membership.

As the United States rejoined in 2023, then US secretary of state Antony Blinken said it was key Washington was present at UNESCO for decisions “that actually matter”, including on “rules, norms and standards for artificial intelligence”.

China was among countries to oppose the move.

World.title: ‘Close ties with Crown Prince’: Sri Lankan MP seeks PM Modi’s help for release of Tamil youth accused of blasphemy in Saudi

The lawyer has also informed the embassy that the judgment could be appealed before Saudi Arabiaâs Supreme Court within one month. The embassy, in consultation with the ministry, is taking steps to pursue the appeal in coordination with Sivarasaâs family.

Sri Lankan Tamils account for around 12-13% of the island nationâs population of more than 20 million and are mainly concentrated in the Northern and Eastern provinces.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Mamata Banerjee's Rejinagar pick withdraws from bypolls contest, then retracts
World.content:
Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction's candidate for the Rejinagar Assembly bypoll, changed his decision to quit the contest on Saturday, saying he would remain in the race after Banerjee asked him to continue.

Chowdhury, a former TMC MLA, had announced his withdrawal earlier in the day, citing difficulties in protecting party workers and introducing voters to the faction's newly allotted 'footballer' symbol.

Hours later, he held another press conference and said he had reversed his decision after speaking to Banerjee and receiving assurances of security from the police.

Candidate changes his mind

Chowdhury told news agency PTI at his home in Murshidabad earlier on Saturday, "It is becoming difficult for me to motivate grassroots workers who have been facing regular harassment.

Also, it is an onerous task to familiarise the electorate with the new 'footballer' symbol in such a short time. In this given situation, last night I informed Mamata di about my decision (not to contest)... Let's see," he said.

Later, he announced that he would contest the October 6 bypoll.

"I will be contesting the bypoll. I have been assured of security by the police after the supremo (Banerjee) intervened... I had a conversation with our party chief, who directed me not to quit the poll fray.





I have met officers of the Beldanga police station and they have also assured me and my cadre of security during campaigning."

"I am retracting from my earlier decision. I will see to it that none of our workers faces torture. Even if I have 10 activists, I will win," he added.

Nandigram setback came first

The confusion in Rejinagar came a day after the Mamata faction suffered a setback in Nandigram, where its candidate Sanchita Pradhan Dey withdrew her nomination shortly before the deadline.

Dey had met West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari at the state secretariat Nabanna along with her husband Satyajit before pulling out. She had lost her job in connection with a teacher recruitment scam. The reason for her withdrawal was not immediately clear.

With no candidate left, Banerjee announced support for Congress nominee Milan Pradhan, calling the Congress a "sister party" and saying the move was aimed at strengthening the INDIA bloc ahead of the October 6 bypoll.

Pradhan was later arrested in connection with criminal cases filed against him during the 2007 anti-land acquisition movement in Nandigram.

TMC split complicates bypoll battle

The developments have unfolded amid a bitter dispute within the Trinamool Congress over its name and traditional 'flowers-and-grass' symbol.

The Election Commission has allotted Banerjee's faction the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' and the 'footballer' symbol.

The rival faction led by Arup Roy has been given the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and the 'envelope' symbol.

Banerjee's camp accused the BJP government of "acting in an authoritarian manner to crush dissent and win the bypoll by a huge margin".

With Chowdhury now back in the contest, the Mamata faction has retained its candidate in Rejinagar, while the Nandigram contest remains shaped by the withdrawal of its original nominee and its subsequent support for the Congress candidate.

World.title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: Employees hid question papers in shoes, paid Rs 8,000 each
World.content:
File photo: Thane Police arrest three in connection with TET paper leak case

How the papers allegedly got out

Leak exposed a day before exam

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test should be rescheduled immediately? Yes, as soon as possible No, wait for the investigation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles, with two employees paid Rs 8,000 each to smuggle out the confidential examination material, according to a chargesheet filed by Thane City police.The chargesheet, filed before a Bhiwandi court on Friday, names 18 accused, including alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta, and lays out how investigators traced the leak from the printing press to those allegedly trying to sell the papers in Maharashtra. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while two others, Ashok Sav and Prakash Misal, remain absconding, police said.According to the chargesheet, the leak was traced to Mahim Patran Pvt Ltd, an Agra-based printing press tasked with producing the confidential TET examination material.Between June 15 and 17, two employees and a former staffer allegedly concealed folded question papers inside their shoe insoles while leaving the premises. Security guards frisked their clothes but allegedly did not check their footwear, allowing the papers to be taken outside, the chargesheet said.The state had prepared four separate sets of question papers for the two TET papers to maintain confidentiality and allow one set to be selected on examination day.Investigators allege that all four sets were nevertheless taken out of the press.The employees were allegedly paid Rs 8,000 each and promised land plots in Agra in return for stealing the papers, according to the chargesheet.The racket came to light on June 27, a day before the TET was scheduled to be held. Deputy commissioner of Police Pavan Bansod received information that three men were allegedly trying to sell question papers to a Bhiwandi resident.Police then laid a trap using decoy personnel in Kongaon and detained the suspects, recovering four sets of question papers. Officials of the Maharashtra state council of examination later verified that the seized material matched the actual TET paper.The examination, scheduled for June 28, was subsequently postponed.Police have booked the accused under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy, along with Maharashtra laws dealing with examination malpractice. A special investigation team is probing the case.Investigators have identified Gupta, a former coaching-class teacher, as the alleged mastermind. Police said he had previously been implicated in another examination paper leak in Odisha.The chargesheet cites money trails, technical evidence and the recovery of an original question paper from the Bihar residence of a relative of Gupta as evidence in the alleged supply chain. Police said a supplementary chargesheet would be filed as the investigation continues.

World.title: 'Delhi a terrifying daily story for women': Rahul, Priyanka slam Amit Shah over teen's gangrape-murder
World.content:
Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

What happened in Delhi case

NEW DELHI: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl in Delhi, with both questioning the authorities over women's safety and demanding accountability for the incident.Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, criticised the Delhi Police and questioned the responsibility of Union home minister Amit Shah, under whose ministry the force functions. He said the teenager was gang-raped and murdered before her body was dumped in an open field, and questioned how the police remained unaware of the crime for days.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi described the incident as a "horrific act of brutality" in the national capital. He also dismissed the idea that Delhi was providing women with a safe environment, saying the city had instead become a source of fear for women."It's unfortunate that Delhi is no longer the capital today; it has become a terrifying daily story for women," he said.Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. He pointed out that the Delhi Police is under the Union home ministry and asked who should ultimately be held responsible for the safety of women in the capital."Amit Shah ji, Delhi Police is under your control. Ultimately, whose responsibility is women's safety?" he said.He also criticised the functioning of the Delhi Police, asking whether its role had been reduced to intimidating ordinary citizens while criminals continued to operate without fear."Or has the job of Delhi Police been reduced to just intimidating and threatening ordinary citizens? Because the criminals are roaming around fearlessly," Gandhi said.Calling for immediate action, the Congress leader demanded that those responsible for the crime be arrested and punished strictly. He also sought accountability for what he described as criminal negligence."The beasts must be arrested immediately, strict action and punishment must be taken, and accountability for this criminal negligence must be fixed," he said.Rahul Gandhi ended his post by linking women's safety to India's wider progress, saying, "India cannot move forward without women's safety."Priyanka Gandhi also raised concerns over the case, saying the crime against the teenager represented an extreme form of brutality. She noted that another minor girl had allegedly been raped just days earlier and questioned whether authorities were taking sufficient responsibility for women's safety."In Delhi, all limits of cruelty were crossed against a 17-year-old girl, and after that, she was brutally murdered. Just a few days earlier, another minor girl was raped," she said in a post on X.Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women. She argued that while there was discussion about women's development, women continued to face violence without what she described as concrete action against perpetrators."No one in the country is willing to take responsibility for women's safetyâonly empty talk about women's development is offered," she said.She claimed that hundreds of women face atrocities and violence and alleged that victims can struggle to get action from authorities, including the registration of FIRs."Hundreds of women face atrocities and violence, but they cannot hope for concrete action against the perpetratorsâFIRs aren't even filed," she said.Priyanka Gandhi also said the issue went beyond the individual case and reflected a wider failure to ensure women's basic rights. She argued that both society and the government had failed to provide women with adequate safety, freedom and equality."Both society and the government have completely failed in granting women their rights to safety, freedom, and equality," she said.A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field, with the police facing questions over the delay in detecting the crime.The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital, with Rahul Gandhi focusing on the Delhi Police's role and its accountability to the Union home ministry.Priyanka Gandhi also referred to another case involving a minor girl that was reported days before the teenager's rape and murder. She used the two incidents to question the wider response to crimes against women.

World.title: Ladakh groups call off week-long protest march

World.title: Sri Lankan lawmaker seeks Modi’s intervention in Saudi case involving Tamil youth
World.content:
A Sri Lankan opposition lawmaker on Saturday (September 19, 2026) urged President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to seek Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's intervention in the case of a minority Tamil youth facing judicial proceedings in Saudi Arabia.

The appeal concerns Anojan Sivarasa, a Sri Lankan national, whose family has claimed that he was sentenced to death in Saudi Arabia over a social media post allegedly amounting to blasphemy.

Sri Lanka's Foreign Ministry has, however, not confirmed that Sivarasa has been sentenced to death.

“I urge President @anuradisanayake to bring #Anojan_Sivarasa’s desperate plight to the urgent attention of your friend, recipient of ‘SriLanka Rathna’ Prime Minister Narendra Modi,” Tamil Progressive Alliance leader Mano Ganesan said in a post on X.

“Given PM Modi’s close ties with Saudi Prime Minister and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, I appeal to you to ask PM Modi to personally intervene with Crown Prince Salman and seek a humanitarian resolution for Anojan,” Mr. Ganesan added.

<Appeal to President> I urge President @anuradisanayake to bring #Anojan_Sivarasa's desperate plight to the urgent attention of your friend, recipient of "SriLanka Rathna" Prime Minister Narendra Modi.



Given PM Modi's close ties with Saudi Prime Minister and Crown Prince… pic.twitter.com/4wFbn1RoZh — Mano Ganesan (@ManoGanesan) September 19, 2026

Sivarasa is a minority Tamil from Sri Lanka's Eastern Province, officials said.

He is a resident of Natpittimunai in Kalmunai, and travelled to Saudi Arabia for employment nine months ago, the NewsFirst media portal reported.

The Sri Lankan Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Friday (September 18, 2026) said: “The Ministry remains engaged with the relevant Saudi authorities through diplomatic channels and is taking appropriate steps to safeguard Mr. Anojan Sivarasa’s interests and provide him with all possible assistance.” it said in a statement.

Sivarasa has been initially sentenced to five years in prison and fined three million Saudi riyals after being found guilty of posting social media content deemed insulting to a religion, the Daily Mirror newspaper reported.

Sivarasa's lawyer later verbally informed the Sri Lankan Embassy in Riyadh that the sentence had reportedly been enhanced to capital punishment, according to the report.

World.title: U.S. lifts sanctions targeting Eritrea's ruling party and the military
World.content:
The United States lifted sanctions against Eritrea's ruling party and the military that the Biden administration imposed, according to the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

The sanctions were issued in 2021 over humanitarian and human rights concerns in the northern Ethiopian region of Tigray, which suffered violent conflict at the time. Eritrean forces backed Ethiopian troops against fighters loyal to the regional government of Tigray in the conflict that ended with a peace accord in November 2022.

The Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control said in a Friday (September 18, 2026) statement that sanctions against some Eritrean individuals, including Hagos Ghebrehiwet, a key financial official, have been removed. The state-owned Red Sea Trading Corporation was also on the list.

Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel said the sanctions had been unwarranted and caused considerable damage to his country.

“In this respect, we welcome the gesture and remedial measures by the Trump Administration,” Mr. Gebremeskel told The Associated Press.

The sanctions delisting comes amid heightened concern about security in the Red Sea.

Recent Houthi advances in Yemen have increased threats to shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, while Eritrea's southern coast and the port of Assab lie near the strategic passage connecting the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.

World.title: Keralam power crisis: Suresh Gopi says previous governments too responsible, asks public to ‘wait’ before judging UDF
World.content:
Union Minister Suresh Gopi has said that he did not intend to criticise the United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Keralam for the ongoing power crisis, as previous governments were also responsible for the current situation.

“You should ask why such a situation (power crisis) emerged. The previous governments were also responsible for it,” he told mediapersons on the sidelines of the Union government’s Rozgar mela held in Kochi on Saturday.

He said that it is not yet time to criticise the performance of the UDF government. “Let us wait,” he said. He rejected allegations that there is a deal between the UDF government and the Bharatiya Janata Party.

He reiterated that he failed to get support from the previous Left front government when he tried to bring in tourism projects for the State. “It has changed now. The hurdles were cleared after it was brought to the notice of the Chief Minister. That should not be portrayed as a deal, as such allegations are raised by people with vested political interests,” he said.

On the corruption allegations in the CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case, Mr. Gopi said that it is up to the courts to take a decision on such cases.

World.title: Entry to Kambathrayan Giri temple restricted on Purattasi Saturdays over recent forest fire
World.content:
Entry to the Kambathrayan Giri Perumal temple in the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve (STR) has been restricted on Purattasi Saturdays following a recent forest fire in the hill area.

In a release, the Forest Department said the restrictions had been imposed in the interest of public safety and forest protection. The fire had damaged grasslands and small vegetation, while rocks in some areas remained highly heated. Burnt vegetation, loose soil, and rocks could pose a risk of slips, falls and falling rocks, it said.

Only tribal people and local residents from the Sathyamangalam and Kadambur areas will be permitted to visit the temple for worship on Purattasi Saturdays. They must obtain permission from the Forest Department and produce valid identity cards.

Visitors have been advised to enter the forest between 9 a.m. and 11 a.m. and leave by around 3 p.m. People from outside these areas have been prohibited from entering the hill area for safety reasons.

Photography banned

Photography and videography have also been prohibited in the protected forest area. The department warned that legal action would be taken against those violating the restrictions and posting photographs or videos on social media.

Visitors have been instructed not to smoke, consume alcohol, light fires, carry inflammable materials or throw plastic and other waste in the forest. They have also been asked not to approach, follow or disturb wild animals.

The Forest Department appealed to visitors to follow the safety instructions and cooperate with its personnel. The fire, which broke out on September 1, was doused after three days of intensive efforts by more than 100 Forest Department personnel, with support from local people.

World.title: India's FTAs opening new career opportunities for youth: PM Modi
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (September 19, 2026) said that the Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) signed by India with various countries are opening new doors to career opportunities for the youth.

Addressing a 'Rozgar Mela' (Jobs Fair) virtually, the Prime Minister also said that the talent and skills of India's youth have won the trust of the entire world, which has great expectations from Indian innovators, entrepreneurs and the country's youthful strength.

"India signed 40 Free Trade Agreements. These FTAs are opening new doors of possibilities for our youth. Such trade agreements pave the way for new partnerships for our entrepreneurs, open paths to new markets, and create new possibilities in careers for our youth," he said.

At the function, the prime minister distributed more than 51,000 appointment letters virtually to newly selected youth, who will join various government departments and organisations.

Referring to the just concluded BRICS Summit, Mr. Modi said India's effort has been to ensure that BRICS cooperation does not remain limited to governments alone.

"Our entrepreneurs, our farmers, our women, our youth — everyone should become an active partner in this partnership," he said.

Referring to the country's startup ecosystem, the Prime Minister said India's youth power is reflected in it and the startup ecosystem is no longer limited to big cities but has expanded to other cities as well.

"India is today the world's third largest startup ecosystem. And India's startup story is no longer just the story of big cities. Today, nearly half of recognised startups are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities," he said.

Mr. Modi said the country is moving forward toward a very significant goal of building a developed India by 2047.

"In this, young people like you have a very significant role to play. While serving in the government, you must make every decision that continuously strengthens the campaign for a developed and self-reliant India. Being young, you have a special responsibility, particularly towards other young people," he said.

The Prime Minister said 'Nagrik devo bhava' (citizens are god) should be the guiding spirit of public service.

As many as 45 'Rozgar Melas' (job fairs) were held at locations across the country.

The newly recruited candidates will join various Ministries and departments of the central government, including the Department of Revenue, the Ministry of Railways, the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the Department of Financial Services and the Ministry of Defence, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office.

The Rozgar Mela reflects the government's continued focus for creating employment opportunities for youngsters and ensuring their greater participation in the country's development journey, an official statement said.

With the 20th Rozgar Mela, 12.75 lakh youngsters have received appointment letters in various departments and government organisations, it added.

World.title: Youth dies of electric shock during Vinayaka idol immersion
World.content:
A private electrician, K. Bharat Kumar (19), died of electrocution while connecting electric cables during Vinayaka idol immersion in Jinkapalem village, Nagayalanka mandal in Krishna district.

World.title: Vinayaka idol immersion: Restrictions imposed on movement of vehicles in Puducherry town
World.content:
The police have imposed restrictions on the movement of vehicles in Puducherry town to facilitate the smooth conduct of the procession carrying Vinayaka idols for immersion near Beach Road on Sunday (September 20, 2026).

The immersion of idols will take place on the beach front near the Old Court Complex on Sunday evening. Restrictions on the movement of vehicles, mainly along Kamaraj Salai, Anna Salai, S.V. Patel Salai, Ajantha Junction, Mahatma Gandhi Road, and Jawaharlal Nehru Street, will come into place from 2 p.m. on Sunday, the police said.

Street area.

All vehicles, including public transport buses and light motor vehicles, coming from the Kalapet side via Muthialpet will have to take the Muthialpet Ezhaimariamman Koil Junction-Sivaji Statue-Rajiv Gandhi-Indira Gandhi Square route, to reach the new New Bus Stand area, a release here said.

World.title: Union Home Minister Amit Shah falls ill in Hubballi, skips inauguration of college
World.content:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who had arrived in Hubballi on Friday (September 18, 2026) night to attend the inauguration of KAHER’s JGMM Medical college, and KLE Hospital and medical Research Centre, skipped the programme on Saturday (September 19, 2026) due to ill-health.

Mr. Shah was supposed to inaugurate the college and hospital at 11 a.m. Accordingly, arrangements had been made and thousands of people were waiting for his arrival at the venue near Gabbur in Hubballi.
